aee5cf30bea46eaa: TOKYO: Former world number one Naomi Osaka said she would "keep attempting" to get back to her Grand Slam-winning best after her season ended with a second-round exit in Japan on Thursday.
The four-time Grand Slam champion lost 6-3, 7-5 to Slovakian 18-year-old Mia Pohankova, ranked 144 in the world, at the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo.
Osaka has not won a title this year and has not reached a Grand Slam final since she returned to tennis after a 15-month break following the birth of her daughter Shai in 2023.
The 29-year-old, now ranked 18 in the world, said she was "at peace" with herself and feeling good about her game.
"Obviously when I play a Slam, it's in my mind to challenge for it," she said.
"Unfortunately I haven't been in that position yet, and I'm going to keep attempting it.
"But if you're asking me how I think my tennis is, I think it's pretty good."
Osaka was appearing at the Pan Pacific Open for the first time in four years.
She came out onto the court wearing a red kimono-style gown with a long frilly train.
She said she chose the colour as a contrast to the blue crane-pattern outfit she wore in her opening match this week.
Osaka said she had more outfits lined up for the Tokyo crowd but "unfortunately" would not have a chance to wear them after exiting the tournament.
Osaka is known for grabbing headlines with her flamboyant custom-made outfits.
She channelled NBA fashion trailblazer Allen Iverson at the US Open and wore an audacious "jellyfish-inspired" outfit in Australia.
She also drew on her Japanese heritage with a kimono-inspired white dress at Wimbledon.
"There are so many things that go on in my mind, and it was just a creative outlet," she said.
"All the other sports are allowed to do that, and tennis is more subdued and restrained."
Osaka started the match with an ace, but former junior Wimbledon champion Pohankova soon turned the tables on her.
The Slovakian, who said she grew up watching Osaka, broke her opponent three times to take the first set and kept the momentum going to win the match.
Pohankova hit seven aces, and Osaka said it was "tricky to play someone that I know nothing about."
"It is a little difficult, but I also remember when I was in her position and I was playing players that I watched on TV," Osaka said.
"I guess age catches up to you eventually."
Canada's Leylah Fernandez progressed to the quarter-finals after beating number five seed Elise Mertens of Belgium 6-2, 7-6 (10/8). - AFP

9b3260583b4c8757: KUALA LUMPUR: The government today signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with six Bersatu MPs and Muar member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, setting out several conditions in exchange for their support.
The seven MPs want the government to limit the prime minister's tenure and separate the roles of attorney-general and public prosecutor before the current administration's term ends.
They also want to receive the same constituency development allocations as government MPs.
In return, the seven opposition MPs will support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's administration until the end of the parliamentary term, including the 2027 Budget.

The confidence and supply agreement (CSA) was signed by Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, Anwar's senior political adviser Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Abdul Aziz, and Syed Saddiq.

The six Bersatu MPs involved in the MoU are Muhyiddin (Pagoh), Datuk Dr Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Datuk Ali Biju (Saratok), Datuk Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Datuk Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
The agreement was also signed by six former Bersatu MPs who were expelled from the party in 2024 after declaring their support for the government.

Anwar previously said allocations could be provided to opposition MPs through a confidence and supply agreement, similar to the agreement reached with the administration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob when Anwar was opposition leader.
The government bloc in the Dewan Rakyat currently has 149 MPs, comprising Pakatan Harapan (PH) with 75 seats, Barisan Nasional (30), Gabungan Parti Sarawak (23) and Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (seven).

Three Warisan MPs are also part of the government bloc, alongside one MP each from Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM), Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (STAR) and Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM).
Eight independent MPs also support the government, including six former Bersatu representatives.
The opposition bloc comprises Pas with 43 MPs, Bersatu (19), Wawasan (six) and Muda (one).
Four seats are currently vacant following the resignations of Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli (Pandan), Nik Nazmi Nik Ahmad (Setiawangsa), Wong Chen (Subang) and Lee Chean Chung (Petaling Jaya).
With 218 serving MPs at present, a simple majority requires the support of at least 110 MPs, while a two-thirds majority requires 146.
bf497c31ea94a75e: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is reviewing the need for further regulatory measures on online gaming platforms, including Roblox, to enhance child protection against digital safety risks.

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC, together with the Communications and Multimedia Content Forum of Malaysia (CMCF), is currently studying online gaming trends and associated risks, including user-to-user interactions, in-game content, and protective safeguards implemented by platform providers.
He said the study also takes into account international practices and frameworks to identify suitable, effective safeguards for implementation in Malaysia.

“At the same time, CMCF is conducting a public consultation to develop a Gaming SubCode involving various stakeholders, including app store operators, local and international game developers, online safety experts, the e-sports industry, legal practitioners, and researchers.

“The findings of this study and consultation will serve as the basis to consider evidence-based, risk-proportional regulatory measures to ensure the safety of users, especially children, continues to be safeguarded,” he said when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage for the Communications Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Fahmi said the government is also prioritising parental education and awareness, particularly on activating parental control functions on personal devices and online services.
He said this initiative is being carried out through the Safe Internet Campaign, which includes the Parent-Teacher Convention and the Safe Internet Campaign Community Carnival nationwide.

The campaign, allocated RM58.7 million under Budget 2027, targets not only students and children, but also provides education and advocacy programmes for parents, guardians, teachers, and local communities.

This collective approach, he added, ensures that the responsibility of protecting children from online threats is shared across families, educational institutions, communities, government agencies, and service providers.

In a related development, Fahmi said 14,706 instances of pornographic content and child sexual abuse material were taken down, while 5,170 pornographic websites were blocked between Jan 1, 2022, and Sept 30, 2026.

Addressing the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) and deepfakes — specifically the circulation of digitally altered nude images involving schoolgirls in Seremban — he said the case remains under investigation by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), with MCMC collaborating closely with the police and platform provider Meta.
MCMC records also showed that 5,341 complaints concerning cyberbullying and online harassment were lodged between January 1, 2023, and October 15, 2026.

Meanwhile, Fahmi said 828,438 online gambling-related posts and materials were taken down, and 7,411 illegal gambling domains were blocked by service providers following directives from MCMC between January 1, 2022, and September 15, 2026.

Enforcement against illegal gambling has also been stepped up through joint operations with PDRM, including Op JOL and Op Soga XI this year, targeting illegal online bookmaking and betting linked to the 2026 Fifa World Cup.

“MCMC has also enhanced operational cooperation with PDRM and telecommunications service providers through Op Pancing and Op Delusi to curb the large-scale dissemination of short messaging service (SMS) spam using Fake Base Transceiver Station (Fake BTS) equipment containing phishing links to deceive users,” he said. — Bernama

9a4c95cc1d057660: HONG KONG: Hong Kong leader John Lee apologised on Thursday for the deadly blaze that killed 168 people in the city last November, promising swift but extensive reforms to its building industry and regulatory system.

Lee was speaking shortly before he released a more than 1,000-page report by the judge-led panel that detailed wide-ranging governance and supervisory failings in Hong Kong's building-renovation system.

Lee also announced the resignation of Hong Kong's Housing Secretary Winnie Ho, echoing the report by saying that four government bodies bore partial responsibility for a blaze that the report said was most likely started by a "glowing source...likely a cigarette."
"As chief executive and head of the government, I am deeply saddened," Lee said in his opening remarks.
"On behalf of the SAR government, I offer my apologies to the victims and the public at large."

Ho was the first official to resign over the inferno. The Hong Kong government has set up an independent team to investigate which officials should be held accountable and to outline disciplinary actions.

Lee said Hong Kong's Chief Secretary Eric Chan will now head a steering committee to oversee reforms advocated in the report, which will include laws to criminalise bid-rigging across the construction industry with fines of up to HK$10 million and 10 years' imprisonment.
The committee report said contractor Prestige Construction & Engineering Co Ltd and project consultant Will Power Architects Co Ltd should bear primary responsibility.

At least 25 criminal charges related to the Wang Fuk Court fire have been made against Prestige, Will Power and seven individuals, including manslaughter, conspiracy to defraud, money laundering and tax evasion.
But the report also went further, outlining widespread unlawful and dubious construction practices as a "corrupt eco-system."
The rigging of bids involved many different parties, some linked to triad organised crime gangs, it said.
"The fire has been put out, but the reform has only just begun," the report stated.
"The Committee finds that no Government department took effective ownership of various fire safety issues and complaints about fire hazards fell into a vacuum," the report stated.
The blaze ripped through seven 31-storey tower blocks at the Wang Fuk Court residential complex, which was undergoing renovation work in the northern Tai Po district.
It was the deadliest in the city since 1948. Thousands of residents were displaced after their homes became uninhabitable.
The committee held 30 hearings this year with 80 witnesses, including residents, property management and renovation personnel, engineering and fire experts, government officials and regulators.
It evaluated more than one million files and submissions as it investigated the cause of the fire and reviewed oversight of building renovations.
692effe7bf6a69da: KUALA KANGSAR: The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, has warned members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court against misusing the Ruler's name, royal influence and their titles for personal gain.

c02963657f129c75: Welcome back to PWNED, in which The Reg offers cautionary tales from folks who’ve left their doors wide open to attackers and lived to tell the tale. This week’s misadventure involves unpatched older machines and a password that was supposed to send a message to crims.
Our story comes courtesy once again of leading red teamer and pen tester Dahvid Schloss of Suzu Labs.

A client asked Schloss to visit a factory and check the servers there for security holes. The company had been hacked six months prior, made some adjustments, and wanted to make sure that they were bulletproof now.
Schloss' mission, which he chose to accept, was to get domain admin rights.

Schloss drove over to the factory where he noticed a number of Windows 7 servers were connected to the CNC milling machines, even though Windows 10 was by then Microsoft's supported desktop OS. This was to be expected, as companies with proprietary software often use legacy OSes for fear of breaking apps.
At first, Schloss had a hard time breaking in because most of the servers were not connected to the domain. So there was no point in his running the EternalBlue zero-day that would have let him in.

“So I've been looking through these and most of them had been disconnected from the domain, so it's the right move,” he said. “Like, yeah, you could run EternalBlue on the network, but you really weren't going to be able to get anywhere with it, cuz you get on the device and what you find: you dump LSASS [the Windows Local Security Authority Subsystem Service], you’re like ‘All right, there’s local admin creds, but the local admin creds on those devices were different from the local admin creds on the majority of workstations.”

Finally, Schloss went onto one of the servers that was connected to milling machines and found that it was connected to the network and on the domain. It was vulnerable to EternalBlue and he went and dumped LSASS and found a pair of creds from WDigest, one of which looked like an admin account.
But Schloss thought that it must not be a legitimate admin account when he read the password : “heyhackergof***yourself,” but written in leet speak [l337 5p34k].

The resulting string was a strong password, but Schloss assumed that the admins were playing a game with him and left this credential there for him to find. Schloss assumed it wouldn't work and sat on it for a week.
During a briefing he had with the IT crew, he presented his findings and then asked who set up the admin account with this funny password.

“You could see everyone kind of looking at the senior manager of IT like ‘that was you, wasn’t it,’” Schloss explained. “He’s kind of got this face. I’m like ‘oh shit, like what?’ Turns out that ‘heyhackergof***yourself’ was the actual password for his admin account."

On Monday, Schloss tried the username and password combo and, lo and behold, it gave him complete control of the entire network. He was then able to get access to other passwords and many of them were also insults directed at potential hackers.

Schloss understood that the team was still angry about a breach they had suffered six months prior and, should they be breached again, wanted to give the finger to the hacker who did it. Unfortunately, their system was still vulnerable because of the outdated machine that was hooked up to the domain and he was able to gain control.
The lesson here is really to patch your systems and avoid using insecure legacy OSes whenever possible, because it was an old machine that let Schloss in, not a weak password.
Indeed, “hackergof***yourself” in leet speak isn’t a terrible password, just an embarrassing one if it's exposed. ®
9424cabcfddf9caa: HPE is giving its Alletra Storage MP X10000 another job: holding inference state that would otherwise be evicted from expensive GPU memory and recalculated later.

In testing validated by Kamiwaza using NVIDIA H200 GPUs, the Kamiwaza AI platform, and HPE Alletra MP X10000, the solution achieved up to 20× faster time to first token and 17× higher effective inference throughput versus running without KV cache offload.
The GPUs did not become cleverer. They had less repeat work to do.

The results move a storage decision directly into the discussion about AI economics. Model pricing gets plenty of attention. Paying expensive accelerators to process the same context repeatedly deserves some too.
Especially as enterprises move from chatbots answering individual questions to agents that can turn one request into a small committee’s worth of activity.
Your agents have a repetition problem

Agentic workflows repeatedly process documents, system instructions and conversation histories. One agent retrieves information, another evaluates it, a third checks the result, and subsequent steps revisit material the system has already processed.
Some repetition is necessary. Recalculating everything is not.

KV cache retains intermediate attention state, allowing compatible requests to reuse earlier computation. Keeping that cache available can reduce the work required before a model starts producing its next answer.
GPU memory, unfortunately, is neither infinite nor priced as though it were.

Long contexts and concurrent sessions compete for that memory. When reusable cache is evicted and later needed, the inference engine may have to rebuild it. More GPU work, more waiting, and no additional insight to show for either.

HPE Alletra MP X10000 provides a shared tier for offloaded cache, while RDMA for S3 accelerates the storage data path. The proposition: retrieve reusable context rather than make the GPU calculate it again.
Compute once. Reuse often. An unremarkable principle, until the alternative appears on the infrastructure bill.
Twenty times faster, with the denominator attached
The Kamiwaza-validated testing used NVIDIA Nemotron 70B and more than 30 concurrent agents under large-context, multi-agent inference.

That matters because this is precisely the sort of real-world workload where repeated context and memory pressure can make cache reuse valuable. Several agents consulting overlapping material create a different opportunity from unrelated, short prompts with little context in common.
Those headline gains are workload-specific. Context length, concurrency, cache hit rates and transfer overhead determine the return. Twenty times faster is a test result, not a universal entitlement.
Buyers should examine the comparison as carefully as the multiplier: the same workload, with and without KV cache offload, and enough concurrency to represent production conditions.
The useful question is how much repeated computation their applications can avoid, and whether retrieving cached context is faster than rebuilding it.
A large performance number without its test conditions is mostly a typography decision.
Garbage in still costs money
Cache reuse addresses repeated computation. It cannot rescue a retrieval system that feeds the model half the company’s document archive to answer one question.

HPE’s broader pitch pairs the X10000 with Data Fabric for governed access to distributed data. The X10000’s data intelligence node generates metadata, classification and embeddings at ingest to help applications retrieve relevant context.
That moves preparation closer to where data lands, rather than leaving every application team to assemble another downstream preparation pipeline.
The economic logic is straightforward. More precise retrieval can mean less irrelevant material in prompts and fewer attempts to obtain a useful answer.
Enterprise archives are rarely short of documents. Distinguishing the current policy from six superseded versions and a presentation called “FINAL_final_v7” is the more interesting problem.

Governance also matters when agents retrieve information and act on it. Relevant context still needs to be authorized context. Faster access to something an agent should never have seen is an awkward definition of progress.
That gives HPE two economic levers: improve what enters inference, then reuse computation where possible.

The distinction matters. Better retrieval can reduce prompt size and retries. KV cache reuse reduces processing work; it does not magically shrink generated answers or oblige an API supplier to lower its bill.
Beyond the cache checkbox
Cache offload is becoming a crowded market. HPE’s strength rests on combining it with data preparation and governance, rather than winning another feature tick.
The practical test for organizations looking to get more value from their AI is how smoothly data preparation, governance and cache reuse operate as a single system.

Can applications find relevant, permitted information without unnecessary copying and preparation? Can the inference engine retain and retrieve reusable context efficiently? Does the combination sustain useful throughput as context windows and agent counts grow?
Those questions connect the architecture to observable outcomes.

Buyers should ask for cache hit rates, time to first token and sustained throughput on their workloads. They should also examine retrieval quality and whether the system completes the intended task. A faster wrong answer remains a wrong answer, however attractive the benchmark chart.
Cost per terabyte remains relevant. So does the cost of making a GPU read the same briefing for the seventh time.
For more information, visit the HPE Alletra Storage MP X10000 web page.

6336b3e55d34d6ef: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has upheld a 17-year jail sentence imposed on a man who took turns with two others to rape their friend's 26-year-old sister-in-law in 2023.
Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin dismissed 31-year-old Nik Khaira Hafizi Mat Zaid's appeal against the sentence imposed by the Sessions Court on June 16, 2024.
In her grounds of judgment, Noor Ruwena said there was no error of fact or law warranting appellate intervention.
She ruled that the punishment was appropriate given the gravity of the offence and the trauma suffered by the victim.
The rape took place at 3.30am on Aug 30, 2023, when four men, including the victim's brother in-law, entered her room while she was asleep.
They restrained her by binding her hands with cellophane tape and stuffed a laundry bag into her mouth to prevent her from screaming.
Nik Khaira and two others took turns to rape the victim while the fourth man helped restrain her and watched the assault.
She tried to kick a window to attract help but was unable to free herself. After the men left, she called 999.
Nik Khaira was charged alongside three men, one of whom was the victim's brother-in-law, who enabled the attack by allowing the other men into the house.
They pleaded guilty after the prosecution had called four witnesses, including the victim.
The Sessions Court sentenced Nik Khaira and two others to 17 years' jail while the fourth man received 14 years.
In the appeal, the National Legal Aid Foundation said the sentencing should consider rehabilitation and a chance to turn over a new leaf.
Deputy public prosecutor Faizal @ Amrin Noor Hadi said the jail term was just.

Noor Ruwena said the aggravating circumstances included the betrayal of trust by the victim's brother-in-law, who had facilitated the crime, and the collective actions of the four men in carrying out the assault.
She rejected the argument that Nik Khaira's status as a first time offender warranted a greater reduction.
"He did not come across (to me) as an immature young offender who may not know the extent of seriousness of the crime," she said.
She borrowed the words of a High Court judge who had said if one was brave enough to tempt fate and get caught, he must be brave enough to face consequences of his act.
9c49768da2d2692d: KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — Malay Reserve Land in Kelantan covers 526,083.08 hectares as of June this year, accounting for 91.58 per cent of the total 574,427.61 hectares of titled land recorded in the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud.
He told the Kelantan State Assembly today that the figure involved 816,020 land titles.
He said Gua Musang recorded the largest area of Malay Reserve Land, at 122,735.54 hectares or 84.55 per cent of the total titled land in the district.

“For the other districts, Kota Bharu recorded 40,510.49 hectares (99.97 per cent), Pasir Mas 56,656.79 hectares (99.98 per cent), Kuala Krai 53,473.85 hectares (68.73 per cent) and Tumpat 21,607.96 hectares (99.99 per cent).

“Bachok recorded 26,541.25 hectares (99.98 per cent), Tanah Merah 56,246.13 hectares (99.98 per cent), Pasir Puteh 43,377.81 hectares (99.99 per cent), Machang 28,376.83 hectares (96.18 per cent), Jeli 37,240.60 hectares (99.93 per cent) and Lojing 39,315.82 hectares (98.99 per cent),” he said in reply to a question from Datuk Mohd Shabuddin Hashim (BN-Galas).

Mohd Nassuruddin said the state government had always given attention to efforts to maintain the area and status of Malay Reserve Land to ensure that the interests of land ownership among the Malays continued to be protected.
He said all development matters involving Malay Reserve Land must comply with relevant legal provisions, including the Kelantan Malay Reservation Enactment 1930.

“Any development matters involving Malay Reserve Land must comply with the relevant laws to ensure that the development carried out does not result in the erosion of Malay land ownership,” he said. — Bernama
10f6ecd8439cc3e5: AMMAN: Jordan Football Association chief Prince Ali bin Hussein said he will cooperate with any Asian Football Confederation judicial review after he accused Fifa president Gianni Infantino of hijacking last week's AFC Congress for political purposes.
AFC president Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim Al-Khalifa had endorsed Infantino for reelection at the continental body's extraordinary congress in Tokyo.

Following the meeting, Prince Ali alleged delegates had not been allowed to speak, question or debate matters and described the final day of the congress as "pure politics at the behest of Gianni Infantino".
Fifa did not respond to a Reuters request for comment on Prince Ali's remarks.

The AFC said on Tuesday that neither Prince Ali nor any other member association's representatives had requested to speak and that allegations involving coercion, threats or bribery should be supported by credible evidence.
It added that it would refer Prince Ali's statements to its judicial bodies.
"I respect the AFC and its judicial bodies and will cooperate fully with any process," Prince Ali said in a post on X late on Wednesday.
"As the Fifa Statutes provide, the Jordan Football Association will cast its vote in the Fifa presidential election independently," he said.
He said his earlier post about the congress was intended to explain the Fifa presidential voting process and highlight the importance of transparency in football governance.

"Its final sentence states a principle the whole football family shares: no election should be open to coercion, threats or bribery. I stand by that principle. It was a statement of principle, not an allegation against any person," he said.
"Where concerns arise, the proper place for them is the competent bodies," he said.
Prince Ali, who has been a vocal critic of Fifa's leadership, said he would make no further comment while the matter remained under consideration.
The AFC did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on Prince Ali's latest post.
Infantino, who has led Fifa since 2016, is seeking reelection in March after apologising for his abandoned proposal to sell a stake in Fifa competitions.
The AFC's endorsement marked a sharp shift from its position three months earlier, when it accused Fifa of a "fundamental breach of trust" over the abandoned proposal.
c8d15fbc0a30604c: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — A Defence Geospatial Information Rapid Team (DGIRT) vehicle has been introduced as a pilot project to accelerate the delivery of geospatial information in the field, supporting defence, security and disaster management operations.

Deputy Minister of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh said the vehicle integrates specialised geospatial equipment to enable faster and more accurate field data collection.

“The vehicle will help us obtain more precise information on the ground while expediting response efforts by enabling teams to reach disaster sites more quickly and accelerating the collection of data and information for follow-up action,” he said.
He was speaking at a press conference after launching Defence Geospatial Day 2026 (DG’26), themed “Advancing Defence and Security Through Geospatial Capabilities”, at Wisma Perwira today.

Also present were Army Chief General Tan Sri Azhan Md Othman, Defence Geospatial Division Director Brigadier General Datuk Dr Mohd Zambri Muhammad Rabab, and Deputy Director-General of Survey and Mapping Malaysia (JUPEM) 1 Ahmad Sanusi Che Cob.

Syed Ibrahim said the vehicle, developed by JUPEM in collaboration with the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM), represented a new initiative, although the equipment and instruments it carries had been used previously, including during the landslide incident in Batang Kali, Selangor.

“The difference is that previously, we did not have a dedicated vehicle that integrated all these specific tools. Now, with this combination of equipment, including electric motorcycles and drones, assessments at disaster sites can be carried out with much greater accuracy,” he said.
He added that the initiative drew on lessons from previous disasters and took into account the operational needs of relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (NADMA).

In his opening address, Syed Ibrahim said geospatial information went beyond mapping, describing it as a strategic national asset essential to strengthening defence preparedness, safeguarding sovereignty and improving the effectiveness of security operations.

He stressed that accurate, integrated and up-to-date information was crucial for supporting decision-making, enhancing situational awareness and ensuring the effective execution of security operations.

At the event, held for the first time in collaboration with JUPEM and ATM, Syed Ibrahim also launched the Defence Geospatial Information Management (DGIM) initiative under the 13th Malaysia Plan (RMK13).
The initiative aims to strengthen the management, integration and sharing of defence-related geospatial information.
He said the development of geospatial capabilities would also involve the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and the exploration of Environmental Intelligence (EI).

Syed Ibrahim further emphasised the importance of cooperation between civilian and military agencies in ensuring coordinated efforts to protect national security and sovereignty, including during humanitarian assistance and disaster management operations. — Bernama
893788cd26805f6e: KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian family travelling in Italy was left distressed after 11 pieces of luggage were allegedly stolen from their car while they stopped for a meal in Pisa.
The incident was shared by Threads user njlaimn, who said a friend and their family were affected while travelling from Pisa to Milan.
The family managed to track their missing iPad to an area believed to be a gypsy camp.
The incident also raised safety concerns, with the family reportedly disappointed by the authorities' response, which fell short of their expectations.
The post drew various reactions from netizens, with some sharing similar experiences and warning travellers against leaving luggage unattended in vehicles.
One commenter advised travellers to head directly from their hotels or accommodation to the airport without making unnecessary stops.

"My advice is to travel directly from your hotel or accommodation to the airport without stopping at other unnecessary places. Never leave luggage unattended in a parked car, even if it is locked," the commenter said.
Another user, farhayayakob, warned travellers against using expensive luggage brands and leaving their bags in a car in a public area.
Another commenter, fakamal, said travellers should make arrangements to transport their luggage to their accommodation before going out to explore.
"Leaving bags like that in a car is practically inviting thieves in Italy. Make the effort to send your luggage to your accommodation first, then go out sightseeing," the user wrote.
Other netizens expressed sympathy for the family and hoped their difficulties would be eased and that they would return home safely.
11fbd05e91032694: KOTA KINABALU: Pelbagai perancangan sedang digerakkan bagi mencapai sasaran Keluaran Dalam Negeri Kasar (KDNK) Sabah sebanyak RM100 bilion menjelang 2030 di bawah agenda pembangunan Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ), kata Ketua Menteri Hajiji Noor.

Beliau berkata fokus kini adalah untuk memastikan perancangan pembangunan industri, menarik pelaburan dan penyediaan infrastruktur dilaksanakan, termasuk menjamin bekalan tenaga yang stabil, boleh dipercayai dan mampu milik.

“Apabila pelabur mempertimbangkan untuk membina kilang atau menjalankan operasi berskala besar di Sabah, mereka perlu mengetahui sama ada kita mampu menyediakan bekalan elektrik dan gas yang mencukupi, berapa kosnya serta bila bekalan itu dapat disediakan,” katanya pada majlis perasmian Persidangan Perancangan Tahunan Sabah Energy Corporation (SEC) hari ini, menerusi teks ucapan yang dibacakan oleh Pembantu Menteri kepada Ketua Menteri Ceasar Mandela Malakun.

Hajiji berkata, bekalan gas Sabah berpotensi meningkat daripada kira-kira 700 juta kaki padu standard sehari kepada 1,350 juta kaki padu standard sehari menjelang 2030, berdasarkan Pelan Pembekalan dan Penghantaran Gas Jangka Panjang yang dibentangkan kepada kerajaan negeri pada September lepas.
Katanya, cadangan pembangunan sumber gas di Pantai Timur Sabah turut membuka peluang baharu bagi penjanaan elektrik dan pertumbuhan industri di wilayah itu.
Kerajaan negeri juga mencatat kemajuan dalam memperkukuh penyertaan Sabah dalam sektor tenaga menerusi Perjanjian Kerjasama Komersial (CCA) dengan Petronas yang dimeterai pada Disember 2021.

Beliau turut memuji prestasi kewangan SEC dan usaha syarikat itu mengembangkan operasi menerusi Agenda Transformasi Tenaga Progresif (Peta 2030), sambil menggesa syarikat berkaitan kerajaan (GLC) dan agensi negeri memperkukuh kerjasama bagi mempercepat pelaksanaan projek serta mengelakkan peluang pelaburan terlepas.
6c6f10d08205e0e7: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Datuk Seri Siti Nurhaliza has revealed she narrowly escaped broken teeth and a split lip after a nasty rehearsal fall left her face bruised and injured.

The 47-year-old singer said she was counting her blessings after the accident, which saw her fall face-first onto the floor while preparing for her Konsert Tradisional Gema Bumantara earlier this month.
Although her injuries are healing, Siti revealed that some bruising remains and the affected tissue on her face still feels unusually hard.
“Alhamdulillah, my face is gradually recovering. The bruises are almost gone, but because I have sensitive skin, blue bruises like these take a long time to disappear.
“My facial tissue still feels quite hard, possibly due to the impact of the fall. I need to massage the area to help with the recovery,” she told mStar, The Star’s Malay-language portal.
The singer said she went straight to hospital for a CT scan following the mishap, but was relieved when doctors ruled out fractures and internal bleeding.

“After I fell, I went straight to the hospital for a CT scan. Alhamdulillah, there were no fractures or internal bleeding. The doctor did tell me that the bruises would take time to fade and that the tissue on my face had been injured,” she said.
Siti was speaking to reporters at the Majlis Tahlil Tun Hasmah event at Yayasan Kepimpinan Perdana in Putrajaya yesterday.
The accident happened during rehearsals for her October 17 concert, when a stunt involving a long piece of fabric went painfully wrong.
Footage of the incident showed the singer attempting a jump using the fabric as a prop before her foot became caught, sending her tumbling face-first onto the floor.
She suffered small cuts near the outer corner of her eye and beneath it, along with bruising on her right cheek.
But Siti said things could have been far worse had she landed differently.

“Alhamdulillah, Allah was still protecting me. I am thankful that I did not fall forward. If I had, my teeth could have broken, my lips could have split, and everything would have taken even longer to heal,” she said.
Despite the frightening mishap, the veteran performer went on to sing at her concert, with the injuries failing to derail the show.
“Alhamdulillah, I was still able to sing and complete my concert. I am grateful to Allah. This was the first time I had fallen during a concert,” she said.
Siti, who previously shared a photograph of her bruised face on Instagram Stories, said she was thankful that the concert went ahead successfully despite the scare.
“I am grateful that even though I fell, Allah protected me. Alhamdulillah, the concert was also a great success,” she added.
06fd938de0b67cac: PETALING JAYA: Criminal proceedings against an accused who dies before trial must be recorded as having abated, rather than ending in a discharge or acquittal, the High Court in Johor Bahru has ruled.
Judicial Commissioner Avinder Singh Gill said the law did not contemplate continuing a prosecution against someone who had died, as criminal proceedings are personal to the accused.
“The proceedings do not survive the accused. They abate upon his death,” he said in a ruling arising from a joint drug trafficking case.
The court was considering what order should be made after the second accused, Fairuz Omar, died on Sept 21 while awaiting trial.
The prosecution had sought a discharge amounting to an acquittal under Section 254 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
However, Avinder said such a discharge presupposes a living accused who could potentially be prosecuted again.
He also rejected a discharge not amounting to an acquittal (DNAA), saying death was neither temporary nor surmountable.

“To import the DNAA/DAA (discharge amounting to an acquittal) terminology into the situation of a deceased accused is to force the statute and the authorities to do work for which they were never designed.”
He added that recording an acquittal could wrongly suggest the deceased had been cleared after a trial on the merits.
The court ordered the case to proceed against the three surviving accused, with trial fixed for March 23 to 26, 2027.
Avinder said the prosecution may amend the charges to remove the deceased's name.
acc7ffd0d4a64704: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Bersatu has signed a confidence and supply agreement (CSA) with the Madani government, pledging its support for the Supply Bill 2027, or Budget 2027, The Star reported.

According to the English daily, Bersatu president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin said the agreement would allow the party’s MPs to receive the same constituency development allocations as government backbenchers.
“I signed on behalf of Bersatu and there are also the other six who previously showed support to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“There are also matters concerning institutional reforms, including proposals to limit the Prime Minister’s tenure to a maximum of two terms and to separate the powers of the Attorney General.
“In return, the government has decided to provide our MPs with the same constituency development allocations as government MPs,” he told reporters after the signing ceremony at Parliament.
Muhyiddin said the agreement followed a similar arrangement during the administration of former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob, when Anwar was the opposition leader.
“Its sole purpose is to create a more stable situation in the country so that important matters affecting the people, particularly the economy and cost of living, can continue to be addressed.

“With this agreement, stability can help the government manage the country more effectively. We, particularly Bersatu and the opposition, will continue to fulfil our responsibility to provide checks and balances.
“This agreement does not mean we are giving up our responsibility as the opposition. We remain the opposition,” he was quoted as saying.
Asked what would happen if either side breached the agreement, Muhyiddin said the terms provided for such a situation, the report said.

“If something has been agreed upon but is not adhered to, the party concerned, whether the government or the political party, may take action, which could lead to the termination of the CSA we signed today,” he was quoted as saying.
Asked why Bersatu had signed the agreement now, nearly a year before Parliament is due to be dissolved, Muhyiddin said the party had hoped for such an arrangement from the beginning.
“Today, I am the only one who has signed it. There are one or two other parties on the opposition side, and I do not know why they have not entered into an agreement. That is their issue.
“From the beginning, we had asked for all MPs to be given equal allocations. When I was prime minister, allocations were given to all MPs, from both the government and the opposition.
“But under the current Prime Minister, he said perhaps the time had not yet come. Today, that time has come,” he said.
The Star reported that Muda’s Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman was also involved in the signing, which was facilitated by Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof.

Also present were Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said and Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki.
Bersatu vice-president Datuk Seri Ahmad Faizal Azumu, Putrajaya MP Datuk Radzi Jidin and Langkawi MP Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah were among those attending the ceremony, according to the report.
20577440e7cca0c8: PORT KLANG, Oct 29 — The full implementation of the Multi-Lane Free Flow (MLFF) toll collection system is expected to help address the issue of toll evasion, including by identifying motorists who commit such offences.

Minister of Works Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said the Ministry of Works (KKR), through the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), continuously monitors the efficiency and effectiveness of toll systems nationwide which are developed by highway concession companies.

He noted that initiatives currently being implemented by these concession companies include toll payment technology based on Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR), which is aimed, among other things, at reducing traffic congestion.
“Therefore, the implementation of the Multi-Lane Fast Flow (MLFF) system at toll plaza lanes will also assist in obtaining information regarding individuals who commit toll evasion.

“This, in turn, facilitates the tracking of such offenders and enables claims to be made against them should they evade detection,” he said at the launch ceremony for the Westports-Public Works Department (JKR) Klang Road Safety CSR Initiative at West Port, here today.

On October 23, the media reported that the concessionaire and operator of the Kuala Lumpur–Karak Expressway (KLK) and the East Coast Expressway Phase 1 (LPT1) incur losses over RM20,000 annually due to persistent toll evasion.

AFA Systems and Services Sdn Bhd general manager, Ismaliza Ibrahim was reported as saying that his organization records approximately 3,000 instances of toll evasion per year with an average of eight cases daily.
On October 13, Alexander said artificial intelligence (AI) technology would be incorporated into the MLFF system once it is fully implemented.

Under Section 8 of the Federal Roads (Private Management) Act 1984, individuals found guilty of toll evasion face a fine of no less than RM2,000 and no more than RM5,000, or imprisonment for up to one year.

Alexander acknowledged that toll evasion has been an ongoing issue though it involves a relatively small number of cases and noted that his team is currently working closely with enforcement agencies, such as the Road Transport Department (JPJ) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), to address the matter.

Regarding preparations for Northeast Monsoon season (MTL), Nanta said his ministry is in a state of full readiness, which includes enhancing the effectiveness of the Disaster Operations Room (BiGBen).
“Through this operations room, we remain prepared to conduct monitoring to identify any disasters particularly floods in affected locations,” he said.

Meanwhile, Nanta noted that the primary objective of the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) programme with Westports is to improve awareness and safety within the port area, which sees the daily movement of nearly 80,000 vehicles, including a large number of heavy machines.
“Measures include the installation of road studs, rumble strips, and warning signs, as well as the implementation of proper lighting, road markings, and effective speed management.
“Furthermore, we are considering a proposal to provide dedicated lanes or paths for motorcyclists, who account for the highest number of accident victims in the area,” he said. — Bernama
31b9a78c99ec0eec: KUALA LUMPUR: Presiden Bersatu Muhyiddin Yassin berkata perjanjian keyakinan dan perbekalan (CSA) yang dimeterai dengan kerajaan persekutuan hari ini tiada kaitan dengan kemungkinan kerjasama pilihan raya antara parti itu dan Pakatan Harapan (PH) pada PRN Melaka.
“Itu perkara berasingan. Ia tiada kaitan dengan perjanjian ini,” katanya kepada pemberita selepas majlis menandatangani perjanjian itu di Parlimen hari ini.
Muhyiddin berkata demikian ketika ditanya sama ada Bersatu kini akan menjalinkan kerjasama pilihan raya dengan PH di Melaka.
Spekulasi mengenai kemungkinan kerjasama kedua-dua pihak timbul selepas pemimpin PH dan Bersatu menghadiri jamuan tertutup di Melaka pada 28 Sept.
Bagaimanapun, cadangan itu mendapat tentangan daripada beberapa pihak dalam PH.
Muhyiddin turut berkata CSA yang dimeterai hari ini berasingan daripada perjanjian seumpamanya yang sedang diusahakan antara Bersatu dan kerajaan Selangor pimpinan PH.
“Itu perkara lain. Perjanjian ini adalah antara kerajaan persekutuan yang diwakili perdana menteri dengan Ahli Parlimen daripada parti saya serta parti lain yang terlibat,” katanya.
CSA itu membabitkan enam Ahli Parlimen Bersatu dan Ahli Parlimen Muar Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Menerusi perjanjian itu, mereka mahu tempoh jawatan perdana menteri dihadkan serta peranan peguam negara dan pendakwa raya dipisahkan sebelum tamat penggal kerajaan.
Mereka turut menuntut peruntukan pembangunan kawasan sama seperti yang diterima Ahli Parlimen penyokong kerajaan.
Sebagai balasan, tujuh Ahli Parlimen pembangkang itu akan menyokong pentadbiran Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim sehingga tamat penggal Parlimen, termasuk menyokong Belanjawan 2027.

Enam Ahli Parlimen Bersatu yang menandatangani perjanjian itu ialah Muhyiddin (Pagoh), Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Ali Biju (Saratok), Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) dan Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).
Perjanjian itu turut ditandatangani enam bekas Ahli Parlimen Bersatu yang dipecat pada 2024 selepas menyatakan sokongan kepada kerajaan.
Muhyiddin berkata tandatangan mereka sekadar formaliti kerana mereka sebelum ini sudah menyatakan sokongan kepada perdana menteri.
Menurutnya, Bersatu akan kekal sebagai pembangkang dan terus memainkan peranan semak dan imbang walaupun selepas CSA itu dimeterai.
Muhyiddin berkata perjanjian berkenaan dijangka kekal berkuat kuasa sehingga Parlimen dibubarkan, tetapi boleh ditamatkan sekiranya mana-mana pihak gagal memenuhi komitmen masing-masing.
Ditanya mengapa CSA itu hanya dimeterai kira-kira setahun sebelum Parlimen dijangka dibubarkan, Muhyiddin berkata Bersatu sebenarnya mengharapkan perjanjian sedemikian sejak awal.
“Sebagai contoh, ketika saya menjadi perdana menteri, semua Ahli Parlimen sama ada kerajaan atau pembangkang menerima peruntukan.
“Namun, di bawah perdana menteri sekarang, maklum balas sebelum ini ialah mungkin masanya belum sesuai. Sekarang masanya sudah tiba, jadi kami menandatangani perjanjian ini,” katanya.

Sementara itu, Syed Saddiq berkata CSA itu perlu disusuli dengan undang-undang yang menjamin peruntukan pembangunan kawasan secara adil dan sama rata kepada semua Ahli Parlimen, bukan hanya mereka yang menandatangani perjanjian tersebut.
Beliau berkata perjanjian itu menetapkan peruntukan kepada Ahli Parlimen kerajaan dan pembangkang mestilah sama, walaupun jumlah sebenar belum didedahkan.
“Perjanjian itu menyatakan peruntukan untuk Ahli Parlimen kerajaan dan pembangkang mestilah sama. Itu perkara yang sangat penting,” katanya.
Syed Saddiq turut menggesa supaya kemudahan itu diperluaskan kepada semua Ahli Parlimen pembangkang kerana peruntukan yang adil adalah hak setiap kawasan Parlimen.

aa977401910e0514: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 29 — Sabah is pursuing various initiatives to achieve a gross domestic product (GDP) target of RM100 billion by 2030 under its Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development agenda, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.

He said the state government was focusing on implementing industrial development plans, attracting investments and providing essential infrastructure, including a stable, reliable and affordable energy supply.

“When investors consider building a factory or conducting large-scale operations in Sabah, they need to know whether we can provide an adequate supply of electricity and gas, what the costs will be, and when such supplies can be made available,” he said.

Hajiji said Sabah’s gas supply had the potential to increase from approximately 700 million standard cubic feet per day to 1,350 million standard cubic feet per day by 2030, based on the Long-Term Gas Supply and Transmission Plan presented to the state government last September.
He added that the proposed development of gas resources along Sabah’s east coast would create new opportunities for power generation and industrial growth in the region.
Hajiji also highlighted progress in strengthening Sabah’s participation in the energy sector through the Commercial Collaboration Agreement (CCA) with Petronas, signed in December 2021.
He commended SEC’s financial performance and its efforts to expand operations through the Progressive Energy Transformation Agenda (PETA 2030).
He also called on government-linked companies (GLCs) and state agencies to enhance cooperation to accelerate project implementation and prevent investment opportunities from being lost. — Bernama
a56b334b23ea3538: TUARAN, Oct 29 — The Sabah government is strengthening youth participation in policymaking through initiatives such as the Chief Minister’s Young Thinkers (Pemikir Muda) initiative and the Sabah Youth Assembly, providing platforms for young people to contribute ideas on the state’s development.

Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor said youths were not only future leaders but also key economic drivers and agents of change in realising the aspirations of the Sabah Maju Jaya (SMJ) development plan.

“Meanwhile, the Sabah Youth Assembly serves as a platform for youth unity and representation, providing a space to discuss issues and the future of the young generation under a new implementation format overseen by the relevant ministry,” he said.

Hajiji said RM98.06 million had been allocated to the state’s Ministry of Youth Development, Sports Advancement and Creative Economy this year to empower young people through various forms of assistance, funding and skills training.

He said the allocation covered human capital development, grants for youth associations, support for the sports sector and assistance for young entrepreneurs through the Sabah Youth Entrepreneur Success Scheme (Syabas).
It also included the Rumah Mesra SMJ initiative, which provides support for young people who have recently started families.

Hajiji added that the state government was strengthening youth skills through Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) to meet the needs of future industries and nurture a generation capable of creating employment opportunities.

On the Tuaran Youth Tamu Carnival, he said the event highlighted the role of young people as future leaders in society and the state, as well as strategic partners in advancing economic, social and community development.

He said the carnival drew on the traditional tamu concept, which brings together traders, small-scale entrepreneurs, farmers, artists and local communities, while providing young people with opportunities to exchange ideas, showcase their talents, expand their businesses and build collaborative networks.

35eec45d08db9fb9: LONDON: British energy giant Shell said Thursday that its net profit more than doubled to US$12.1 billion in the third quarter as the Middle East war disrupted supplies and sent oil and gas prices soaring.
The company had posted profit after tax of US$5.3 billion in the third quarter of 2025.

"Shell's relentless focus on operational performance enabled very strong results in a quarter with continued severe disruption to the global energy system," chief executive Wael Sawan said in a statement.
Revenue rose sharply to US$92.8 billion from US$68.2 billion in the same period a year earlier.
Shell's refining margins, reflecting the spread between the price of crude oil and the fuels derived from it, surged to a record high in the quarter as the Middle East and Ukraine wars hit supplies.
The production and export of refined products in the Middle East have remained heavily disrupted since the war began in late February.
Logistical constraints have complicated the re-routing of fuel supplies, widening the gap between crude oil prices and refined products.
At the same time, Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian energy infrastructure have prompted Russia, a major player in the oil market, to ban the export of certain products, notably gasoline and diesel.
Refineries unaffected by the conflict are thus benefiting from the tightening global supply of such products.
Profit margins reached US$42 a barrel in the third quarter, up from US$24 a barrel between April and June.
At US$42, the level is far above the previous record set in 2022, just after the invasion of Ukraine by Russia, according to Bloomberg.
Shell also said it would boost its share buyback programme to US$5 billion.
5f9d007aaf1899f4: KOTA BHARU, Oct 29 — The Kelantan state government today tabled a RM1.383 billion Budget 2027, comprising RM1.087 billion in operating expenditure and RM296 million for development.

“The difference between projected revenue and operating expenditure indicates a deficit of RM4.31 million.

f6921c4afd211929: KUALA LUMPUR: Bersatu president Muhyiddin Yassin said the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) signed with the federal government today had nothing to do with a possible electoral pact with Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the Melaka polls.
“That is a separate question. That has nothing to do with (the agreement) here,” he told reporters after the signing at Parliament today.
Muhyiddin was responding to a question on whether Bersatu would now be forming an electoral pact with PH in Melaka.
Speculation of a tie-up with Bersatu emerged after leaders from both sides attended a closed-door dinner in Melaka on Sept 28. However, the matter has faced pushback within PH.
Muhyiddin also said today's CSA was separate from a similar agreement being sought between Bersatu and the PH-led Selangor government.
“That is another matter. This agreement is between the federal government, represented by the prime minister, and MPs representing my party and the other parties involved,” he said.

The CSA involved six Bersatu MPs and Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, with the MPs seeking a limit on the prime minister’s tenure and the separation of the attorney-general and public prosecutor's roles before the end of the government’s term.
They also want to be allocated the same amount of constituency development funds that government backbenchers currently receive.
In return, the seven opposition MPs will support Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s administration until the end of the parliamentary term, as well as the 2027 budget.

The six Bersatu MPs who signed the agreement are Muhyiddin (Pagoh), Radzi Jidin (Putrajaya), Ali Biju (Saratok), Suhaimi Abdullah (Langkawi), Nazri Abu Hassan (Merbok) and Azman Nasrudin (Padang Serai).

The deal was also signed by six former Bersatu MPs who were sacked in 2024 for declaring support for the government, with Muhyiddin saying their signing was merely a formality as they had already expressed support for the prime minister.
Bersatu would remain in the opposition and continue to provide checks and balances despite the agreement, he said.
Muhyiddin also said the CSA is expected to remain in force until Parliament is dissolved, but could be terminated if either party failed to honour its commitments.
Asked why the deal came a year before Parliament is due to be dissolved, he said Bersatu had hoped for such an agreement from the start.
"For example, when I was the prime minister, all MPs, whether from the government or the opposition, received allocations," he said.
"Under the current prime minister, however, the response was that perhaps the time was not right yet. Now, the time has come, so we signed the agreement."

Separately, Syed Saddiq said the CSA must lead to legislation guaranteeing fair and equal constituency development allocations for all MPs, rather than benefitting only those who signed the agreement.
He said the agreement specified that allocations for MPs on both sides must be equal, although the exact amounts had not been disclosed.
“It states that allocations for government and opposition MPs must be equal. That is a crucial line,” he said.
He also called for the agreement to be extended to all opposition MPs, saying fair allocations were the right of every parliamentary constituency.
ed56fc24b372c4a3: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Asean member states should not allow overlapping maritime claims in the South China Sea to fracture the peace and solidarity in the region, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said.
Speaking at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM), Mohamed Khaled said the Asean solidarity is one of the bloc’s greatest strengths that must be preserved.

“The South China Sea represents one of the most consequential tests of Asean’s unity, credibility, and commitment to its founding principles,” Mohamed Khaled told his Asean counterparts in Cebu, the Philippines yesterday.
“Several member states have overlapping maritime claims, and each has legitimate interests in safeguarding its sovereignty and territorial rights.
“But no dispute, however deeply rooted, should be allowed to fracture Asean or undermine the peace we have spent decades building,” he said.
Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam, Brunei, China and Vietnam have competing claims over territories in the contested waters.

Asean and China signed a non-binding Declaration on the Conduct of Parties (DoC) in 2002 and talks for a binding Code of Conduct (CoC) have been underway since 2013. Both parties are reportedly expecting to finalise the CoC by end of this year.
Stronger regional disaster response capability needed
As the region increasingly grapple with the ravages of climate change, Mohamed Khaled said Asean requires a stronger, more coordinated and effective regional disaster response capability.
He pointed out that Asean already has essential mechanisms in place, such as the Asean Militaries Ready Group on Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (AMRG on HADR).
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Asean Defence Ministers’ pose for the symbolic Asean handshake at the 20th Asean Defence Ministers’ Meeting in Cebu, the Philippines. — Picture courtesy of Ministry of Defence (Mindef)

The mechanism provides a framework to coordinate military assistance and facilitate the deployment of military assets to disaster-affected areas, which was reflected in Asean’s response to the devastating earthquake in Myanmar last year.

“We must now build upon these foundations to strengthen operational readiness, improve coordination and ensure that our armed forces can respond swiftly and effectively when disasters strike,” he said.
Confronting new threats
Established in 2006, the ADMM marked its 20th anniversary this year under the chairmanship of the Philippines with the theme “Navigating Our Future, Together”.
As such, Mohamed Khaled called on the ADMM to develop strong local and regional capacity to respond to new non-traditional threats effectively.
“The threats confronting Asean today are more complex, more interconnected, and potentially more destructive than ever before.
“We must acknowledge that non-traditional threats are no longer distant possibilities. These threats are real, recurring and increasingly difficult to ignore,” he said.
Mohamed Khaled also reminded his counterparts that Asean member states cannot effectively combat the evolving security challenges by working in silos.
“No Asean member state, regardless of its resources, can address these challenges entirely on its own.
“Asean’s future cannot be secured by any one member state acting alone.
“Our strength rests on the trust we build among ourselves, our willingness to manage differences constructively, and our determination to uphold the wider interests of the region,” he added.
bd0af15811d187dd: MALAYSIA'S environmental approach rests on the National Policy on the Environment (DASN), which promotes sustainable resource use and the Environmental Quality Act 1974 (EQA), providing a legal basis for pollution control.

Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 13, 14 and 15 address climate action, marine ecosystems and life on land. Malaysia also participates in the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP), recognising that some environmental risks cannot be managed within national borders alone.

The challenge is turning these commitments into practical protection for communities and essential services. The priority is to make existing arrangements work together, rather than assume that additional policies or institutions will solve the problem.

The November 2020 Sungai Selangor pollution incident shows how an environmental problem can quickly affect daily life when four water treatment plants temporarily stopped operating, disrupting supplies in parts of the Klang Valley.
Although authorities responded, the interruption shows why shared information, clear responsibilities and early preventive measures matter.
Protecting a water source is also about maintaining the service it provides.
Some threats extend beyond Malaysia's control. Transboundary haze can affect health, schools and economic activity even when fires occur outside the country.
AATHP provides a basis for cooperation, while the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) shares hotspot and weather assessments.
Regional progress therefore depends on countries sharing information promptly, examining conditions on the ground and acting on common assessments within their own legal powers.
Environmental monitoring also offers an opportunity to act earlier. Malaysia and Asean already use monitoring networks, satellites and location-based information.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) could help connect these sources, identify unusual patterns and support forecasts.
However, an alert is useful only if its reliability can be checked and someone has the authority to respond. Poor data, false warnings and cybersecurity risks can weaken confidence.
AI should assist experienced officials, not replace their judgement or legal responsibilities.
Across these examples, the central issue is the link between knowledge and action.
Policies set priorities, agencies protect services, regional partners share information and monitoring tools identify risks.
National resilience improves when these functions support timely, coordinated decisions rather than operate separately.
To address these weaknesses, we should establish a Malaysia Environmental Security Resilience Framework (MESRF).
It rests on Policy and SDG Integration, Governance and Regional Cooperation, and AI-enabled Environmental Intelligence.
Its guiding principle is to connect existing institutions before creating new ones.
Four initiatives would put the framework into practice.
First, develop a set of Environmental Security Indicators to show where environmental pressures threaten people and essential services.
Second, federal and state agencies should agree on practical procedures for sharing risk information, checking warnings and deciding who should act.
Third, strengthen the operational value of Asean cooperation by exchanging timely information, conducting joint assessments where appropriate and reviewing responses after regional warnings.
Fourth, an AI-Enabled National Environmental Intelligence Platform (AI-NEIP) could be explored as a decision-support tool connecting environmental, satellite and geospatial data.
Environmental security is ultimately about keeping communities and essential services functioning when environmental conditions deteriorate.
Malaysia already has sound policies, laws, regional partnerships and monitoring capabilities. Their value depends on how effectively information moves between institutions and leads to action.
Success should be judged by earlier credible warnings, better coordinated prevention and fewer avoidable interruptions to essential services.
Stronger national resilience begins with making existing capabilities work together.
* The writer is Assistant Commissioner of Police, Royal Malaysian Police and currently attending the National Resilience College at the National Centre for Defence Studies (PUSPAHANAS), Putrajaya

3b6c5d3ce181f034: BEIJING: Sanrio, the Japanese company that owns the popular Hello Kitty character, apologised Thursday over its tie-up with a TV spy drama criticised as anti-China, cancelling a merchandise collaboration with the show.
It comes after Chinese sponsors dropped football superstar Kylian Mbappe over comments calling communist leader Mao Zedong a "dictator", which the Real Madrid forward later apologised for.

"We have recently received feedback from various quarters regarding the collaborative merchandise with the Japanese television drama VIVANT," Sanrio's Chinese unit said on social media platform Weibo.
"We sincerely apologise for any concern this may have caused," the post said.
The project "contains expressions that are inconsistent with the Sanrio Group's corporate philosophy", it said.
Sanrio said it had "decided to cease this collaboration, as well as all subsequent projects and promotional campaigns."
In one episode of the TV drama, a Chinese-affiliated organisation had been depicted torturing a member of the Japanese military's unofficial spy unit.
Chinese state media outlet The Global Times had called the show "notorious for smearing China", saying it had sparked shock and fierce backlash on social media."
The series reflects the "anti-China narrative of the current conservative Japanese right-wing administration, catering to the trend of right-wing extremism in Japanese society", it said.
Contacted by AFP, private broadcaster TBS, which created the drama Vivant, could not immediately comment.

The network's president told Japanese media that the drama is "a fictional entertainment work" and that TBS "does not in any way take a position that foments conflict between nations or condones the use of force or violence."--AFP

086f7503e2a915aa: BATU KAWAN, Oct 29 — The Penang Island City Council (MBPP) has submitted a draft technical report on the recent landslide at Taman Seri Permai, Paya Terubong, to the state government, said Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow.
He said the report was still being followed up and reviewed before a detailed report on the incident could be finalised.

“Several possible causes of the incident have been identified for further investigation by the technical authorities, including weather conditions, surface runoff, drainage pipes and excessive soil load.

“However, we do not want to speculate. A detailed explanation should come from the engineers, and the state government is also still awaiting the full report from MBPP on the incident,” he told reporters after opening Estek Automation’s new factory here today.
In the incident at 8.36am last Sunday, a 73-year-old doctor, Wong Kar Lin, was killed after being buried in a landslide that hit his home.

Chow said matters related to technical planning would be handled by state Local Government and Town and Country Planning Committee chairman H’ng Mooi Lye, while the welfare of affected residents would be coordinated by state Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai, who is also the Paya Terubong assemblyman.
He said the developer had been in contact with the affected residents to assess their accommodation and welfare needs.

Commenting on calls for the state government to halt all development projects involving high-risk slopes, Chow said such a move could have legal implications as the developers had obtained the relevant approvals and commenced work.
He said project approvals were granted based on procedures and conditions stipulated by the relevant authorities and agencies, including technical agencies.

Meanwhile, Chow said the state government had directed all relevant agencies to remain on standby throughout the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), particularly in anticipation of possible flooding following heavy rain.

He said September to November was typically a period of high rainfall in Penang, and all agencies therefore needed to take appropriate action based on information received from the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) whenever it rained.

The 2026/2027 MTL began on October 27 and will continue until March 2027. According to the Malaysian Meteorological Department, three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain are expected from November this year to January 2027.

This could increase the risk of flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying areas, while strong winds could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the waters of the South China Sea. — Bernama
120cdb92ecc5d984: KUALA LUMPUR: Property developer Parkland Bhd has received approval from the Securities Commission (SC) for its initial public offering (IPO) and proposed listing on the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia.
The IPO will comprise 621.54 million shares, representing 26.3 per cent of the group's enlarged issued share capital of 2.36 billion shares upon listing.
It will comprise a public issue of 468.14 million new shares and an offer for sale of 153.40 million existing shares.
Of the total IPO shares, 550.74 million will be made available to institutional and selected investors, as well as Bumiputera investors approved by the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.
The remaining 70.80 million shares will be offered to the public through balloting, as well as eligible employees and persons who have contributed to the group's success.
Proceeds from the public issue will be used mainly to acquire landbanks and fund working capital for the group's developments.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd is the principal adviser for the IPO and, together with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, will act as joint placement agent and joint underwriter.
Parkland, which develops integrated townships and residential properties in Johor, Melaka and Selangor, has a planned development pipeline worth RM5.05 billion as at May 25, 2026.
About 75.5 per cent of the pipeline is located in Johor.

With 18 years of experience in construction and property development, Parkland has launched integrated townships and standalone property projects with a total gross development value (GDV) of RM7.4 billion across the launched phases.
Its ongoing developments include the Taman Kluang Perdana, Taman Bukit Perdana, Taman Parkland and Bandar Layangkasa townships, as well as Parkland by The River in Johor.
In Melaka, its projects include the Bandar Botani Parkland township and Parkland Avenue by The Sea development.
Parkland has also ventured into renewable energy through a joint venture with Xinyi Power Station Development (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Hong Kong-listed Xinyi Energy Holdings Ltd.
The joint venture has secured the development of a 99.99-megawatt large-scale solar plant in Tangkak, Johor, which is expected to begin commercial operations in the first quarter of 2027.
Group managing director Datuk Tan See Sen said the SC's approval marks a significant milestone in Parkland's journey towards listing on the Main market.
"The proposed IPO will provide us with a stronger platform to accelerate our development plans, expand our land bank and further strengthen our position in the property development industry.
"Moving forward, we remain committed to leveraging our established presence in Johor, Melaka and Selangor while pursuing strategic opportunities that support the group's long-term growth," he said.
c6e0de62b351f312: PETALING JAYA: Four men pleaded not guilty at the Johor Bahru sessions court to setting fire to a house occupied by Rohingya refugees in Kulai.

Yap Eze Hong, 31, Amirul Eizlan Musrinan, 28, Khairul Abd Bahrin, 27, and Chan Jie Mig, 28, were charged with committing arson at a house in Lorong 5, Kulai Besar, Kulai, at 1.30am on Oct 13, Sinar Harian reported.
The charge under Section 436 of the Penal Code carries a jail term of up to 20 years and a fine upon conviction.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Aisyah Latiff handled the prosecution. Yap was represented by lawyer GK Sritharan, Khairul by Siti Rashidah Abd Aziz and Chan by Chon Sin Lim. Amirul was unrepresented.
Aisyah sought bail of RM25,000 each, but defence lawyers appealed for a lower amount, citing their clients’ irregular income, reliance on daily wages and the need to support their families.
Judge Che Wan Zaini Che Wan Ibrahim set bail at RM8,000 for Yap and Chan, and RM10,000 for Amirul and Khairul.
The court also ordered them to report to the nearest police station every month, surrender their passports and refrain from harassing victims and witnesses.
The case will be re-mentioned on Nov 30 for document submission.
c8e1c32616134209: OCTOBER 29 — Having a decent roof over your head isn’t just about comfort, it is about survival and opportunity.

It determines whether a family loses their entire life savings when the monsoon waters inevitable rise, or whether a wage worker can live close enough to their job to avoid spending hours in traffic each day.

Malaysia has understood the task and over the past few decades, the country has made remarkable progress in expanding access to housing, most recently pushing past national targets by delivering more than 511,000 affordable housing units under the Twelfth Malaysia Plan.
Large-scale public housing programmes, urban upgrading efforts and investments in infrastructure have helped improve living conditions for many communities.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

The author argues that adequate housing goes beyond providing shelter, calling for safe, affordable, climate-resilient and well-connected homes supported by inclusive urban planning and community involvement. — Unsplash pic

Yet new challenges continue to emerge such as rapid urbanisation, with the national urban population now exceeding 75 per cent, changing demographics, rising living costs and climate-related risks are reshaping what Malaysians need from housing today.
As we celebrate this Urban October under the theme “Adequate Housing for All”, the question is no longer simply whether a family has a roof over their heads.
The more important question is whether that home is safe, affordable, resilient, well-connected and able to support a decent quality of life.
For Malaysia, as for the world, ensuring adequate housing is central to building inclusive, resilient and sustainable cities.
Globally an estimated 2.8 billion people face some form of housing inadequacy, and close to 1.1 billion live in slums and informal settlements.
As climate change intensifies, the need for resilient housing, risk-informed planning and safer urban development becomes increasingly important.

Malaysia is increasingly integrating climate resilience into housing and urban development policies through nature-based solutions, resilient infrastructure and risk-informed planning approaches that seek to protect vulnerable communities while improving urban liveability.

Recognising these challenges, the country recently launched the National Housing Policy 2026-2035, which emphasises housing affordability, a more responsive relationship between housing supply and local demand, stronger housing data systems, integration of housing and transport planning, and the development of a more formal and regulated rental ecosystem.
The policy reflects an important shift: adequate housing is being recognised not only as a matter of construction, but also as a matter of urban liveability, inclusion and long-term resilience.
A decade after world leaders adopted the New Urban Agenda (NUA), the verdict is clear global progress if falling far behind schedule, Member States recommitted to these goals through 2036.
Malaysia’s evolving housing agenda positions the country to lead by example to the NUA commitments.

Having hosted the Ninth World Urban Forum (WUF9) and taking on the Presidency of the UN-Habitat Assembly for 2025–2027, Malaysia is no longer following international frameworks, is actively shaping them.
Global goals only matter if they make a difference on your street.
That is where UN-Habitat and URBANICE Malaysia focus their work, helping cities and states turn big international commitments into practical local plans.
One way they do this is through Voluntary Local Reviews and Voluntary Subnational Reviews.
These are health checks that cities and states carry out on themselves.
They measure how well they are doing on the Sustainable Development Goals, the targets the world has agreed on for ending poverty, protecting the planet and improving lives.
With UN-Habitat’s support, Malaysian local authorities have used these reviews to see where they stand, plan with real evidence and bring more voices into decision-making.
URBANICE Malaysia also helps cities learn from one another.

Through the Malaysia Urban Innovation Hub, public forums and hands-on support for local councils, it connects people who are solving similar problems in different places, so a good idea in one town can take root in another.
All of this comes back to a simple point: a home doesn’t stand alone.
It needs a bus stop nearby, clean water, a safe park, jobs within reach and protection from floods, and some of the best ideas come from residents themselves.
At Malaysia Urban Forum 2026, held under the theme “The Future City I Want to Call Home”, community members, young people and researchers shared practical ideas for better places to live.
The Ministry of Local Government Development (KPKT) is now funding three community-led pilot projects to put some of those ideas into action.
It is a reminder that people who live in a place usually know best what it needs.
Urban October invites us to remember that adequate housing is about people, opportunity and dignity.
When every Malaysian has a home that is safe, affordable and connected, we build stronger communities and a future we can all call home.
* Srinivasa Popuri is the Chief of the UN-Habitat Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific
