a730a691b9fd747b: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 29 — Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) is offering a record 1,573,872 seats for its Electric Train Service (ETS) and Ekspres Rakyat Timuran (ERT) from January to March 2027, a 39 per cent increase over the same period this year.
In a statement today, KTMB said ticket sales for both services will open in stages from November 2, allowing the public to plan travel ahead of school holidays, public holidays and festive seasons.
Ticket sales for ETS and ERT travel between January and February 2027 will open at noon on November 2, while tickets for March 2027 travel will go on sale on December 1.
According to the statement, of the total seats on offer, 1,520,592 are allocated to ETS and 53,280 to ERT.
“The figure exceeds the 1,131,500 seats offered for the same period in 2026, making it the highest number KTMB has ever provided for the first three months of the following year,” the statement read.
“This increase in capacity reflects KTMB’s ongoing efforts to provide more travel options to meet the needs of rail service users,” it said.
ETS ridership is projected to grow 6.5 per cent to 6.28 million passengers in 2027 from 5.9 million this year, matching the capacity increase.

With demand rising, KTMB will increase ETS service frequency in 2027 from 44 scheduled services a day in 2026 to 50 services a day from Monday to Thursday and 58 services a day from Friday to Sunday, an increase of between six and 14 services a day.
The higher frequency also covers the JB Sentral- KL Sentral- JB Sentral route, where services will rise from eight to 12 a day.
The move is expected to offer passengers more schedule options, particularly on weekends and during peak seasons.

In addition, KTM announced that the Old Kuala Lumpur Station and Subang Jaya Station will become additional ETS hubs, widening rail access and offering alternative stations to ease congestion at KL Sentral during peak hours and busy seasons.
In a related move, KTMB will restructure its long-distance ETS timetable from Jan 1, 2027, affecting several routes linking the northern and southern sectors of the network.

“Direct through-travel on the same train for the JB Sentral-Butterworth, JB Sentral-Padang Besar and Butterworth-Segamat routes, and in the reverse direction, will no longer be offered. Passengers on these routes must change trains at KL Sentral,” the statement said.
KTMB said tickets for long-distance ETS services requiring a train change at KL Sentral must currently be bought in two separate transactions, one per travel sector.
However, KTMB is upgrading its booking system to allow integrated purchases in a single transaction from December.
Passengers are therefore advised to check schedules for both ETS services and ensure sufficient transfer time at KL Sentral before booking.

The public is encouraged to buy tickets early via the KITS Style app or the official KTMB website at www.ktmb.com.my, and to check the latest schedules before booking, particularly for long-distance trips requiring a train change at KL Sentral. — Bernama

3febd51f7fa5ec6a: SINGAPORE, Oct 29 — You’ve probably seen people doing the viral Chongqing motorcycle trend on social media — where they ride pillion and pose with style against the city’s nightscape.
But for Singapore content creator Cheryl Tay and her travel companion, the experience isn’t quite as enjoyable as it appears on screen.
“We both did the viral motorbike trend in Chongqing and we didn’t have a very good experience,” she said in a TikTok post on Tuesday.
According to Cheryl, it all started when the two of them were approached by a woman near Hongya Cave in Chongqing who offered them a chance to take part in the activity.

Before agreeing to it, the content creator said she asked a few questions — such as whether she would be able to ride the motorcycle herself and if she could choose which partner to ride with — all of which the woman apparently answered yes to.

After paying a deposit and arranging the appointment, Cheryl and her friend were then picked up by another man at the designated meeting point and brought to an office to change into their outfits for the shoot.
However, Cheryl was less than impressed with the clothes provided, which she said were “a bit smelly”.
“I don’t think that they washed it properly,” she said.
“I felt like I had a hundred people’s sweat on me.”
After getting dressed for the occasion, the pair was then brought to a roadside, where they met the rider who would be doing the shoot with them.
And that was when things really started going downhill.
According to the content creator, they were repeatedly being rushed throughout the experience.
At one point, her friend said that a helmet was even forced onto her.

“They were prioritising volume over quality, and it came off in their body language, in the way they speak, in their attitude. They were very very impatient and it kind of ruined the mood,” said Cheryl.
She added that she even had her own storyline and skit for the video but felt that the rider was not cooperative and made it difficult to execute.
Her friend also described the rider as “extra aggressive” and intimidating, especially because she did not understand Mandarin and was not used to riding motorcycles.
“I feel like he was very military[sic]. Come on! It’s kind of scary if you don’t usually ride bikes,” she recalled.
She further alleged that the rider had handled her roughly while positioning her for the shoot.
Cheryl also questioned why they were being rushed, pointing out that she and her friend had arrived early and were among the first customers of the night.
“Obviously I don’t expect you to roll out a red carpet and treat me like a princess, but I’m just saying basic respect,” she explained.
But despite the negative interactions, Cheryl acknowledged that the final video turned out fine.
However, the duo maintained that the overall experience has been marred by the poor service.

“So, the moral of the story here is, please do your research, please do your homework, go online, search and pre-book,” she urged, suggesting for those interested to get references from people who have done it before.

“Number two, research for the skit you want, such as the storyline, because there’s a standard template of how to do it but you can also change it up a bit and discuss with them prior,” she added, explaining that they did not get to do so as they were being rushed.

In the post’s accompanying caption, Cheryl also highlighted another point of frustration — being told she could not ride the motorcycle herself despite initially receiving the green light from the woman who approached them.
To make matters worse, the content creator claimed that she subsequently discovered they had been overcharged.
“Spend time to do your research and homework! Don’t just go in blind,” she reiterated.

In a separate video posted on Wednesday showing the completed shoot, the content creator said she had initially wanted to switch things up with her carrying the rider and being the driver instead, though it fell through as the vendor was “too commercialised, impatient and rude”.
“The rider made no effort to create chemistry and it left me feeling shortchanged,” she added.
AsiaOne has reached out to Cheryl for more information. — AsiaOne
018b98127c21ad40: KUALA KANGSAR, Oct 29 — The Sultan of Perak, Sultan Nazrin Shah, has warned members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court against misusing the Ruler’s name, royal influence and their titles for personal gain, financial profit or business opportunities.
His Royal Highness also urged them not to allow themselves to be used to assist parties in an improper or questionable manner, or to exert undue pressure on anyone.
“Shun corruption, the abuse of power and any conduct that might give rise to suspicion or tarnish the reputation of the throne and the Royal Court.

“Never allow your position to become a means of seeking special privileges, accumulating personal wealth or interfering in matters beyond the scope of your responsibilities,” he decreed at the 175th Meeting of Dewan Negara Perak at Istana Iskandariah here today.

Sultan Nazrin also urged members of the Dewan Negara Perak and dignitaries of the Royal Court to remain vigilant and exercise sound judgement in communications, particularly when using social media channels and platforms.
“...exercise care and discretion in both word and deed. Matters entrusted to you in confidence must be safeguarded. Information whose accuracy has yet to be established must not be circulated.

“Opinions should be expressed with due propriety, without giving rise to slander or discord. In today’s world, a single remark or recording shared on social media can give rise to many different interpretations,” he said.
His Royal Highness also called on them to avoid disputes, power struggles and factionalism while maintaining close ties with the people.

He said public grievances must be heard and addressed, particularly those involving vulnerable groups such as senior citizens, persons with disabilities, orphans, low-income families and marginalised communities.

“Maintain good relations with people from every walk of life. Our State is home to people of diverse ethnicities, religions and backgrounds. Respect this diversity and work towards strengthening unity, in accordance with the Constitution and the law,” he said.
Sultan Nazrin said members of Dewan Negara Perak and royal dignitaries must understand the role of the monarchy within the framework of a constitutional monarchy.

“Respect the prescribed limits of authority and responsibility. Work professionally with the government and state institutions, without interfering in administrative affairs or using your position to advance partisan political interests,” he said.
The Sultan also encouraged them to continuously broaden their knowledge and improve their ways of working, understand societal changes, and make prudent use of technology.
The Sultan further stressed that every palace dignitary must set an example for their families, officers, staff and the wider community.
“Show that those who are close to the Ruler are equally committed to their responsibilities, and that those who are accorded honour also know how to honour others,” he added. — Bernama
a572a579fa4c31b0: BANGKOK: Thai authorities have vowed to seize more than US$1 billion in assets from a group accused of laundering proceeds from Southeast Asia-based scam syndicates.
A criminal court issued arrest warrants Tuesday for the alleged ring leader, South African Ben Smith, his Thai wife Cattaliya Beevor, Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and four others, police said.

Media reports have previously linked Smith, also known as Benjamin Mauerberger, to transnational scam operations in Cambodia, part of a multibillion-dollar illicit industry that has ballooned in the region.
Yim Leak, who denies the charge, belongs to an elite political family and is the brother of a senior Cambodian police official.
Smith, Cattaliya, Yim Leak and three others have fled Thailand, the country's Securities and Exchange Commission said in a statement.

Thai anti-money laundering officials and securities regulators told reporters Tuesday that illicit proceeds from criminal enterprises were moved by the group through overseas financial firms before being traded for stocks on the Thai stock exchange.

The Anti-Money Laundering Office (AMLO) will seize assets, including shares worth more than 14 billion baht, and real estate, cash and vehicles valued at 21 billion baht, totalling more than US$1 billion, police said in a statement.
The seizures included shares in major Thai firms, including Bangchak, one of the country's biggest oil refiners, according to AMLO deputy head Kamonsit Wongbutnoi.
Bangchak said in a statement that the asset seizures concerned individual investors and business operations were unaffected.
Confiscated assets would go towards compensating victims of online scams, Kamonsit told reporters.
The group of seven were charged with conspiracy to launder money and acting as a criminal organisation, police said.
Lanny Davis, a spokesman for Yim Leak, said the accusations against the Cambodian businessman were "100 per cent false."
"There isn't a shred of truth that he's ever been involved in scam operations in Thailand, in Cambodia or anywhere else," Davis told AFP.
He said Yim Leak denied the charge and challenged the Thai government to provide "any evidence of his knowledge or involvement" in scam operations.
An Oct 8 statement issued by Yim Leak's lawyers accused Thai officials of conducting a trial by media against him before he was charged.
It said Thailand froze more than US$600 million in assets, including his family's, without a hearing.
A lawyer for Smith, Witoon Kengngan, declined to comment on Wednesday.
In February, Thai authorities ordered the seizure of assets worth more than US$410 million from Smith and other individuals accused of fraud.

Thai opposition lawmaker Rangsiman Rome, who is being sued by Smith for defamation over comments he made about scams, told AFP on Wednesday the fresh seizures and arrest warrants were "a positive development... even if it's taken a while."--AFP

51c34f5d752b8887: PARIS: French oil and gas giant TotalEnergies said Thursday that its net profit hit a new record in the third quarter as the war in the Middle East pushed up hydrocarbon prices.
Net profit reached US$8.3 billion in the period from July to September, up from US$5.4 billion in the preceding three months.

"In a high-price environment characterised by historic refining margin levels and a bull gas market, TotalEnergies is once again fully leveraging its integrated business model and its geographic diversification," chief executive Patrick Pouyanne said in a statement.
The company had already reported a strong rise in its bottom line in the preceding two quarters, similarly driven by soaring oil and gas prices as well as its trading activities.
TotalEnergies said the surge in profits would be reflected in a higher dividend for shareholders.

"The board of directors commended the very good operational performance of all business segments which enabled the company to capture higher market prices," the company said in its earnings statement.
The group will undertake a new capital increase reserved for employees, "who will benefit from a 20% discount on the share price".
The board confirmed a third interim dividend of €0.90 per share for 2026, up 5.9% compared to 2025.
TotalEnergies will also proceed with share buybacks for cancellation of US$2.5 billion "for the fourth quarter as well as for the first quarter 2027".
be36abb3dd30ebb7: KUALA LUMPUR: Cadangan membezakan gaji minimum pekerja tempatan dan asing perlu diteliti secara berhati-hati bagi mengelakkan eksploitasi buruh serta teguran Pertubuhan Buruh Antarabangsa (ILO), kata Menteri Sumber Manusia R Ramanan.
Beliau berkata, langkah membezakan kadar gaji berasaskan kewarganegaraan membawa risiko besar terhadap perundangan domestik dan konvensyen antarabangsa khususnya Konvensyen 100 ILO.

Katanya, kerajaan sentiasa komited memastikan keutamaan diberikan kepada rakyat tempatan dalam aspek peluang pekerjaan, termasuk mewajibkan majikan mengiklankan kekosongan jawatan menerusi portal MyFutureJobs sebelum pengambilan pekerja asing dipertimbangkan.

“Namun, sebarang cadangan untuk perbezaan tersebut, khususnya gaji minimum, perlu diteliti secara menyeluruh dan khususnya dari aspek implikasi dan eksploitasi merupakan satu risiko yang kami telah mendapat teguran sebelum ini oleh ILO," katanya ketika sesi penggulungan Belanjawan 2027 di Dewan Rakyat.

Sebelum ini, Lim Guan Eng (PH-Bagan) dilapor mencadangkan dasar kenaikan gaji minimum baharu dihadkan khusus kepada pekerja warga tempatan sahaja bagi mengurangkan beban majikan serta mengelakkan lambakan kos tambahan.

Sementara itu, Ramanan berkata garis panduan keselamatan dan kesihatan pekerjaan bagi pelaksanaan Bahagian 9 Akta Pekerja Gig 2025 (Akta 872) dijangka diterbitkan oleh Jabatan Keselamatan dan Kesihatan Pekerjaan (JKKP) pada November ini.

Garis panduan itu bertujuan memastikan entiti kontrak memenuhi kewajipan seperti menjalankan pentaksiran risiko dan menyediakan persekitaran kerja yang selamat demi mewujudkan ekosistem pekerjaan gig yang mampan.
Beliau berkata, di bawah Seksyen 47(1) akta sama, Majlis Perundingan Gig turut diberi kuasa mengesyorkan formula pengiraan kadar pendapatan minimum mengikut sektor dan wilayah.
Langkah itu disokong kajian menyeluruh kerajaan yang merangkumi 13 siri sesi libat urus, analisis terhadap hampir setengah juta data transaksi individu, serta penandarasan ke atas 42 negara.

"Kesimpulannya, berdasarkan indikator kajian ini, kaedah pengiraan pendapatan dan standard minimum pekerja gig akan dapat dimuktamadkan secara telus, saksama dan bermaruah menjelang awal tahun 2027," katanya.
333b4cb6247840e8: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 29 — The Court of Appeal today granted lawyer Rosli Dahlan leave to commence a judicial review challenging the police and public prosecutor’s move to seize his four Amanah Saham Nasional Bhd (ASNB) accounts under the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA).

A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, Datuk Nadzarin Wok Nordin and Datuk Seri Latifah Mohd Tahar unanimously allowed Rosli’s appeal to overturn a High Court decision that had dismissed his leave application.
The appellate bench ordered the case remitted to the High Court for a full hearing on its substantive merits before a different judge or judicial commissioner.
Delivering the court’s decision, Justice Choo held that the High Court had erred in disallowing Rosli’s application for leave to initiate the judicial review.
Justice Choo said the court was of the view that the High Court judge had applied a level of scrutiny more appropriate to a substantive hearing than to a leave application.
He also said Rosli had demonstrated a prima facie arguable case that the seizure orders may have been affected by mala fide, collateral purpose, irrationality or abuse of power.

“Whether those allegations can ultimately be established is a matter for a substantive hearing. The learned High Court judge therefore erred in refusing leave for this preliminary stage,” Justice Choo said.
Rosli’s lawyer Harvinderjit Singh confirmed the court’s decision to Bernama when contacted.
On August 14, 2024, the then High Court judge Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh (now Chief Justice) dismissed Rosli’s application for leave to initiate the judicial review.

In his application filed in December 2023, Rosli named several respondents, including former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain, Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Seri Ramli Mohammed Yoosuf, the Royal Malaysia Police, former Attorney-General Datuk Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh, deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Zulfadli Mohd Nawawi and the Malaysian government.

Rosli is seeking, among other things, a certiorari order to quash the decision or action of the respondents who issued or caused the issuance of the seizure orders under Section 50 of the AMLA Act 2001.
At today’s proceedings, the Attorney-General’s Chambers was represented by senior federal counsel Normastura Ayub and federal counsel Zulkiefli Sulaiman.
Also representing Rosli were lawyers Chetan Jethwani, Amiratu Al Amirat, Ho Yu Fei and Shavitta Devi Raja Mohan. — Bernama
cf2dc01bb50e62a6: KUALA LUMPUR: FA of Malaysia (FAM) has promised to deliver returns to new title partners Yes and Ryt Bank as the national body seeks to rebuild its image following recent issues.

YTL has previously supported the M-League and is now extending its involvement to FAM, announced under the banner "Demi Bola Sepak Malaysia", the partnership aims to bring supporters closer to the national game.

7148bb521a668510: URDA: Spain began three days of mourning on Thursday after its second high-speed rail collision this year killed 68 people and injured scores, with relatives desperately seeking news about their loved ones.

One of Europe's deadliest train disasters this century has raised fresh questions about safety on Spain's rail network after the transport minister reported an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" that led to the crash.

The collision happened in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha on Wednesday morning when a service by state operator Renfe ploughed into the back of a stationary train belonging to private Spanish company Iryo.

Emergency services combed through the wreckage at night to find further victims on the key line linking Madrid with the southern city of Seville, hoisting pieces of mangled metal with cranes, AFP reporters saw.
At daybreak, police drones were once again flying over the crash site a few kilometres from the small village of Urda
Josimar Medina, a 31-year-old Peruvian who was holidaying in Spain with his girlfriend, said he was sleeping on the Renfe train when "I woke up and I was in the air."
Pablo Mejia, 42, escaped with injuries to his head, telling AFP that a last-minute change of seat saved his life.

Wearing a bloodstained grey jumper and holding his tattered suitcase, he recounted "a very strong hit... a lot of people on the floor, on top of each other, seats ripped out, suitcases, a lot of chaos."
"I think I've been born again," he said.
- 'FINAL MOMENT' -
A school in Urda, around 130km south of Madrid, is being used to allow relatives to enquire about their loved ones.
Teams of Red Cross workers offered support to groups of people who arrived, some of them in tears, amid crowds of police and journalists from around the world.
Red Cross psychologist Carmen Garcia said "long and hard hours" were in store because "every person will manage it in their own way.
"We have people who are in shock, who haven't taken on board what has happened, angry people, sad, worried people. The grieving will be complicated," Garcia said.
The Civil Guard has set up four offices in the cities of Madrid, Toledo, Cordoba and Seville to enable relatives of the victims to provide DNA samples and help identify the missing.
Blood donation points have also been set up in Castilla-La Mancha and Madrid.
Jose Miguel Fernandez, a parish priest in Urda, joined the emergency services in offering support to the victims' families.

"It is important for relatives to find their loved ones, even if they have died, because the grieving process is quicker when you have been able to say goodbye at that final moment," he told radio Onda Cero.
- SAFETY QUESTIONS -
Flags flew at half-mast on public buildings as the country observed a day of mourning, with official ceremonies and public events cancelled or scaled back as a mark of respect for the victims.
Transport Minister Oscar Puente said on Wednesday that an automatic control system went down on 69km of track, causing all trains there to be stopped.
But the control centre decided to "resume traffic in circumstances that, from our point of view, are inexplicable," Puente said, with the Renfe train travelling 25km before striking the Iryo.
The control centre "had more than enough time to verify the error, and they did not fix it", he added.
In January, two high-speed trains collided in the southern region of Andalusia after one of them derailed and crossed onto the adjacent track, killing 46 people.
The investigation into that accident is ongoing, but the left-wing government faced heavy criticism over its management of Spain's railways.

The latest disaster comes one month before Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez seeks to overturn unfavourable polls and extend his eight-year premiership in an early general election on Nov 29.--AFP

63863ecab31bf8cc: BEIJING: In its pursuit of economic self-sufficiency, China must not create one-sided dependence in other markets, Germany's President Frank-Walter Steinmeier urged in an address at a top-tier university in Beijing on Thursday.

b1eefb530b00789d: WASHINGTON: US economic growth likely accelerated in the third quarter (Q3) as resilient consumer spending and AI-driven business investment more than offset the impact of higher oil prices stemming from the conflict in the Middle East.

The anticipated strength would stand in stark contrast to households' downbeat assessment of the economy, reflected in president Donald Trump's record-low approval ratings and a sharp deterioration in consumer sentiment.

The commerce department will publish its advance estimate of Q3 gross domestic product (GDP) on Thursday, less than a week before Tuesday's midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress.
"People are very upset about high energy and food prices, and yet the fundamentals for consumers are still decent," said Gus Faucher, chief economist at PNC Financial.

"We still have job growth, wage gains and there's the strong stock market that's supporting spending by high-income households, in particular, so consumers continue to increase their spending at a pretty steady clip," Faucher said.
GDP likely increased at a 3.2% annualised rate last quarter, a Reuters survey of economists predicted.
The economy grew at a 2.2% pace in the April-June quarter.

However, the survey was conducted before the release on Wednesday of September's advance economic indicators report, which showed a widening of the goods trade deficit as strong demand for capital goods linked to the AI spending boom lifted imports to a record high.
Economists estimated the trade shortfall subtracted at least 4 percentage points from GDP growth last quarter.
However, the drag was probably blunted by the AI-related investment, with business spending on equipment expected to have notched a third straight quarter of double-digit growth.
AI also likely contributed to spending on intellectual property products.
Inventories are also expected to have added to GDP growth last quarter.
Investors are increasingly focusing on the rising costs of long-term AI projects in which the payoff is uncertain.
Tech firms have borrowed huge sums over ​the past year for AI spending, a potential downside risk to equipment spending. Still, economists did not expect this to hinder the economy.
"There's likely to be more discretion when it comes to investment in AI, but the underlying momentum remains quite strong," said Gregory Daco, chief economist at EY-Parthenon.
"AI-related investment is likely to remain a key pillar of US economic activity, even if there are some risks of pullbacks and some questions as to the return on all of its investment," Daco said.
The economy is expanding at a pace that is well above what some Federal Reserve officials regard as the non-inflationary growth rate of around 2%.
The US central bank on Wednesday left its benchmark interest rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range while acknowledging that inflation "remains elevated".

Economists expected the Fed to raise rates in December. Fed chairman Kevin Warsh told reporters that "economic activity is expanding at a strong pace," noting that "while uncertainty remains, owing in part to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient".
Robust consumer spending expected
Consumer spending, which accounts for more than two-thirds of the economy, is projected to have increased at above a 3.0% pace after growing at a 3.8% rate in the second quarter (Q2).
Historic low layoffs and moderate hiring are helping to underpin spending, though wage gains have at times lagged inflation.
Households have been saving less and dipping into their nest eggs to fund spending.
With average gasoline prices still above US$4 a gallon as the US-Israeli war with Iran drags on, economists anticipated that consumer spending would pull back.

"It appears that households made a judgment when the conflict began earlier this year that the run-up in energy prices would prove mostly temporary," said Stephen Stanley, chief US economist at Santander US Capital Markets.
"That assessment may prove wrong, so consumers may need, at some point, to tighten their belts," Stanley said.
Rising mortgage rates because of the Middle East conflict are expected to have pushed residential investment back into contraction last quarter.
Higher borrowing costs have overshadowed a moderation in house prices, putting homeownership out of the reach of young adults.
Homebuilding is also being constrained by land and labor shortages amid an immigration crackdown, and higher prices for materials due to tariffs on imports.
The construction of data centers to support AI likely lifted business investment in nonresidential structures after stabilizing in Q2. A rebound in government spending is anticipated.
A measure of domestic demand, which excludes inventories, trade and government, is expected to have surged last quarter. Final sales to private domestic purchasers grew at a 4.6% rate in Q2.

"The overall picture is that the economy is growing at a decent pace, but the primary factors are an AI-driven investment boom and consumption driven primarily by rising stock wealth," said Dean Baker, senior economist at the Center for Economic and Policy Research.
"It's unclear how long this can continue, but this is not a very stable picture, nor a very positive one for most working people," Baker said.

cb637de114e6e7e1: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 29 — Microsoft shares popped more than five per cent yesterday afternoon after it reported better than expected revenue and profit, fuelled by its Azure cloud computing division which grew by 48 per cent in the September quarter.
“We are delivering greater capability, choice, control, and cost efficiency for customers across our entire stack,” Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said in a statement.
The technology giant recorded US$92.3 billion (RM375 billion) in total revenue and more than US$36.6 billion in profit, the company said in a securities filing yesterday.
Analysts had expected around US$90.6 billion in revenue and US$35.1 billion in profit, according to FactSet.

The quarterly earnings report comes just days after Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant spends heavily on artificial intelligence investments.
It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year, after giving seven per cent of its US workforce the option to retire early in April.
Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings.
Earlier this month, Microsoft also announced a new Surface Ultra laptop that runs on Nvidia’s artificial intelligence chips and will cost more than US$2,500.

The launch is part of a broader push by tech companies to release hardware that can handle more AI computing on-device and offline, so users do not have to rely solely on remote cloud data centres, where running AI is slower and more expensive.
AI spending
One of the big questions looming over tech earnings is whether the industry’s heavy AI spending is paying off.
Analysts are expecting US$51 billion in overall spending by Microsoft from July to September, according to FactSet.
Microsoft nearly doubled its spending on “property and equipment” to US$39 billion compared to the same period last year, according to a press release.
The company added 24 new data centres across the world last quarter, Nadella said on a call with analysts yesterday afternoon.
Its overall capital expenditures reached US$45.2 billion, around three-quarters of which was spent on “short-lived assets” like memory chips and storage, Chief Financial Officer Amy Hood said.
In the final quarter of 2026, Microsoft expects capital expenditures to reach more US$50 billion, which will bring its total spending for the year to US$170 billion, she said.
Microsoft competes with Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Google parent Alphabet for cloud computing services customers.
AWS has dominated the sector and remained number one globally by revenue in the second quarter of the year, according to Synergy Research Group.
Microsoft is number two globally, followed by Google.

However, Google yesterday reported that revenue from its cloud division doubled to US$30.7 billion during the quarter, bringing it closer to Microsoft’s Azure revenue, which reached US$33.2 billion in the same period.
Tech companies are expected to collectively spend hundreds of billions of dollars on AI-related expenses this year.
Tech giants have also been taking on debt to fuel AI growth.
“To complement cash generated by the business and preserve financial flexibility, we will access additional sources of funding when we believe it is attractive to do so,” Hood said.
Alphabet recently raised US$85 billion through equity offerings to fund its AI data centre expansion.
On Monday, Facebook parent company Meta said it would raise US$35 billion through a stock offering to fund its own AI investments.

That stock offering is also a sort of financial carrot intended to keep CEO Mark Zuckerberg in California, where voters in November will decide whether to approve a temporary tax on wealth held by billionaires who reside in the state.
Amazon reports its quarterly earnings today. — AFP
a4a7292cb9d065d2: WASHINGTON, Oct 29 — Shares in Google parent Alphabet fell more than 10 per cent in after-hours trading yesterday as the company reported lower-than-expected profit and a slowdown in its advertising business while it maintained big spending on AI.
Net profit slid 25 per cent from a year earlier to US$26.2 billion (RM106 billion) in the July-to-September period, or US$2.12 per share, well short of expectations by analysts surveyed by FactSet.
Alphabet booked an US$8.7 billion loss on its equity investments, which it attributed to its stake in SpaceX, the Elon Musk-led company where shares have struggled since going public in June.
Revenue rose 25 per cent to US$127.6 billion, slightly below the roughly US$128 billion analysts had forecast.

Advertising revenue grew 11 per cent to US$82.0 billion, short of expectations. Revenue from Google’s search business, still the company’s largest source of income, rose 12 per cent to US$63.4 billion, slowing from 17 per cent growth in the previous quarter.

YouTube, now the most-watched content provider on American TV screens, saw advertising revenue grow nine per cent to US$11.2 billion, down from 13 per cent growth in the previous quarter. YouTube Music and Premium passed 150 million subscribers worldwide, including trials.
Google Cloud, which rents computing power and AI tools to businesses, saw revenue jump 103 per cent to US$30.7 billion, ahead of analyst expectations.
The company said sales of its in-house AI chips, known as TPUs, contributed significantly to that growth. Operating income for the unit tripled to US$11.1 billion.
Google is also selling its TPU chips to outside companies, in a growing challenge to market leader Nvidia. OpenAI plans to buy some of the chips, according to media reports this week.
Alphabet’s “Other Bets” division, which includes robotaxi company Waymo, posted revenue of US$372 million and an operating loss of US$2.0 billion.
Waymo now provides more than 500,000 paid rides per week across 15 US metropolitan areas and aims to reach one million weekly rides by the end of the year.
‘Long-range planning’
Alphabet spent US$51.4 billion on capital expenditures during the quarter, mostly on data centers and AI chips, more than double the US$24 billion a year earlier.
Its latest forecast for capex spending is between US$195 billion to US$205 billion in spending for 2026.
The company said it would continue to increase capex spending significantly in 2027.
“I would broadly think of all of this as a long-range planning process, not a short-term allocation exercise,” Google CEO Sundar Pichai told analysts of the company’s investment splurge.
The company’s spending, which included a fine paid to the European Union, outstripped the cash generated by Alphabet’s businesses for a second straight quarter, leaving a US$9.1 billion gap.
During the quarter Alphabet raised US$28.7 billion by selling bonds and US$12.4 billion by issuing new shares to help pay for its AI ambitions.
Google has stepped up the pace of its AI releases since a delay to a flagship model in July raised questions about whether it was falling behind rivals OpenAI and Anthropic.
It launched Gemini 4 at the end of September and later released a version focused on cybersecurity.
The Gemini app has reached one billion users. Google’s AI models now process nearly 32 billion tokens, or units of text, per minute, more than four times the level of a year ago, the company said.
Anthropic, the maker of the Claude chatbot, is also one of Google’s largest cloud customers. It has committed to using up to one million Google AI chips.
In September, a US judge declined to order Google to sell off parts of its advertising technology business, imposing restrictions on how it operates instead. — AFP
ae9ce9458e24b6f7: BEIJING: Chinese firm Z.AI's flagship AI model carried out complex cyberattacks in controlled simulations and repeatedly ignored instructions in separate tests, according to a report by AI security research firm Irregular.
The GLM-5.3 model successfully completed 3 of 13 multi-stage cyberattack scenarios at least once, the strongest performance Irregular has recorded from an openly available AI model.
GLM-5.3 still trails leading US models in Irregular's tests. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, for example, completed 9 of 10 scenarios in a separate assessment, although the tests were not identical.
The findings underscore concerns that increasingly capable AI models lower the technical barriers to sophisticated cyberattacks.
This is particularly the case with many Chinese AI models like GLM-5.3 that are open-weight, meaning they are available for users to download, modify and operate independently.
Beijing-based Z.AI, one of China's leading AI startups, did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Irregular said GLM-5.3 gained access to protected services, established alternative connections to move through computer networks and coordinated operations across multiple machines during the simulated attacks.
It did not refuse any of the offensive tasks tested.

In separate tests, Irregular found that GLM-5.3 repeatedly reproduced computer code from memory despite being explicitly told not to, allowing it to arrive at correct answers while breaking rules designed to test its abilities.
The researchers described the behaviour as "reward hacking", in which an AI system finds ways to achieve a desired result while disregarding instructions.
They warned that tests measuring only whether a model succeeds could overlook such violations.
Open-weight models popular due to low costs
The findings add to evidence of safety risks emerging in Chinese AI systems.
Reuters last month identified at least 20 studies and evaluations documenting deception, concealed failures and attempts to circumvent restrictions by Chinese-powered AI agents.
That said, unlike rogue AI agent incidents at US companies, there was no evidence they had independently escaped their operators' control.
Leading US companies including OpenAI and Anthropic have largely kept their most powerful models accessible through company-controlled services, making it easier to restrict their use.
In contrast, Chinese developers have embraced open-weight models, which have become popular with developers and companies worldwide due to their malleability and lower usage costs.
Z.AI, also known as Zhipu AI, launched GLM-5.3 in August, having delayed its release by two weeks for additional safety testing.

Anthropic, which has restricted access to its powerful Mythos cybersecurity model over fears of misuse, said in September that GLM-5.3 developed working attacks against software vulnerabilities in 12% of attempts in its tests, compared with 14% for Mythos.
Anthropic also found GLM-5.3's safeguards could be bypassed using relatively simple techniques.

The US National Institute of Standards and Technology has also described GLM-5.3 as the most capable open-weight model for cybersecurity tasks released to date, although it estimated the model lagged leading US systems by around four months.

Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at tech research firm Omdia, said China's AI industry needed stronger checks and balances and more safety testing, adding that he expected the country's leading AI laboratories, which he described as tightly governed, to introduce corrective measures.

b7db9f0c18d3cdc5: A scientist working on data gathered by the Rubin Observatory has found a strong candidate for our solar system’s sixth known dwarf planet.

The Observatory is run by the USA’s National Science Foundation and Department of Energy, who built it on a remote hilltop in Chile and equipped it with the 3200-megapixel Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) Camera, which came online in June 2026.

As explained in a Tuesday announcement, Rubin Operations team member and project contributor Matthew Holman, of the Center for Astrophysics (CfA) at Harvard & Smithsonian, used search code he developed with CfA colleague Kevin Napier to analyze data captured before LSST operations commenced.
The Observatory says Holman’s and Napier’s code “is built to look at billions of detections of moving objects, compare them, and find the detections that correspond to the same object.”
On October 13, the code spotted an object so bright and distant that it is likely unusually large.
“My first reaction was one of excited disbelief,” Holman said. “Objects like this are very rare, so I immediately started checking whether I or the code had done something wrong.”
Other astroboffins sprang into action, dug into other records, and soon found ten years’ worth of relevant data.

Once they all checked their sums, the Minor Planet Center reviewed their work and announced the discovery of the romantically named 2026 ED138 and published lots of data about its orbit, which is at around 46 astronomical units (au). A single au is the distance from Earth to the Sun, and Pluto’s orbit averages 40 au.
Rubin Observatory revealed its part in the effort and declared that 2026 ED138 is a good candidate for certification as a dwarf planet.

The 2026 International Astronomical Union defines a dwarf planet as “an object in orbit around the Sun that is large enough to pull itself into a nearly round shape but has not been able to clear its orbit of debris.”

The Union’s definition of a full planet includes having “an important influence on the orbital stability of the other objects in its neighbourhood.” Dwarf planets whirl about the solar system in relatively close company with many rocky and/or icy objects that orbit under the influence of other bodies, not the nearby dwarf planet.

Rubin boffins think ED138 is between 600 and 1500 kilometers across. If the lower number is correct, it’s the smallest dwarf planet yet observed. Should the larger number be correct, it would be smaller than Pluto, Eris, and Haumea, but larger than Makemake and Ceres.

Scientists at the observatory think ED138 has evaded detection to date because it was found in a region of sky close to the plane of the Milky Way — meaning observers had to pick it out from light cast by billions of stars.

“Rubin Observatory’s regular and continuous monitoring of the entire Southern Hemisphere sky, combined with powerful algorithms that sift through millions to billions of points of light to identify those corresponding to small moving objects, enabled the team to spot ED138 within the crowded field,” the facility boasted. ®

64beab8743078d7b: Japan’s Fujifilm has decided the tape market has so much upside that it needs to boost production of its Linear Tape-Open (LTO) products by five times.
LTO is the sole surviving non-proprietary tape format and is kept alive by HPE, IBM, and Quantum Corp, who head the LTO Program.

As The Register recently reported, shipments of LTO cartridges went backwards during 2025, when buyers shelled out for 160.3 exabytes worth of LTO compared to the record 176.5 exabytes; worth of tape cartridges sold in 2024.
The LTO program attributed the 2025 result to difficult macro-economic conditions, noted that sales picked up strongly in the second half of the year, and predicted record sales in 2026.

Tape users, however, nearly always use it for offline or nearline archives, and understand that access times are not the medium's strong point.

The LTO Program has already defined four more generations of its format and delivers updates about every four years. LTO 11 is therefore due in about 2029 and will reach 70TB capacity. Version 12 will climb to 120TB, before unlucky version 13 shoots up to 210TB. Version 14 will jump to 365TB per cartridge!
The LTO program used to insist that tape drives could read the current past generations of cartridges. That ended with LTO-10 devices, which can only read the current generation of tapes. ®

e639ccd45622ebfa: BEIJING: China's clean technology exports this year will cut carbon emissions outside its borders by an amount equivalent to Brazil's annual emissions from consuming fossil fuels, an analysis finds, ahead of next month's COP31 climate summit.

China's exports of solar panels, wind turbines, electric vehicles and batteries will help the world to avoid 450 million tonnes of planet-warming carbon dioxide emissions, according to the analysis by the Finland-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.
The avoided emissions are equivalent to 2% of the world's annual emissions outside China, which dominates clean energy supply chains from electric vehicles to lithium batteries.
China is the world's largest emitter of carbon dioxide overall, but the US is the biggest per capita emitter and also the biggest historical producer of greenhouse gases. Brazil is a top-10 emitter.
China's clean technology exports are helping the world to avoid emissions especially in the Global South, where they are decarbonising fossil-heavy grids, the analysis found.
The impact of those exports is growing -- avoided emissions are up from 370 million tonnes of CO2 last year, more than the UK emitted from fossil fuel consumption.

The bulk of the avoided emissions came from countries in the Global South, as they have increased imports from China and cleaned up dirty power grids, the analysis found. Many are in sunny regions with rich potential for solar power, by far the biggest source of avoided emissions among China's exports.

The climate savings outweighed the carbon dioxide emitted in manufacturing the solar panels, turbines and other equipment, the report said, estimating it took around six months for clean tech imports to "pay back" the manufacturing emissions.

The amount of avoided emissions over the lifetime of the equipment exported from China in 2026, which in the case of wind and solar farms can be used for decades, is forecast at 8,400 million tonnes of CO2 — as much as the US and India together emit in a year from fossil fuels, the report said.

Despite global concerns about China's industrial overcapacity and its impact on manufacturers in other countries, the analysis found that China's clean tech exports have, in the aggregate, created new markets rather than displacing existing producers.
However, the surge in green exports drove down per-unit prices and cut into the revenues of incumbent producers.
China has labeled clean tech tariffs the new problem for climate action and vowed to push back against them at COP31.

Erik Marmor/picture alliance via Getty ImagesThe Israeli election of Oct. 27, 2026, was among the most highly anticipated votes in the country’s history. It was consequential, if not yet conclusive. With nearly all the votes counted, it is still unclear who will lead the country following the first national ballot since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack, and the devastating wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran that Israel has launched since. The Conversation turned to Dov Waxman, an expert on Israeli politics at the University of California, Los Angeles, to walk us through the main takeaways and the process and difficulties facing anyone trying to form a coalition government following a divided vote. What can we take away from the election results? The first thing to note is simply the massive turnout – with a 77.7% turnout of those eligible voting, the highest turnout in more than two decades. That in itself is significant. It underscores how much importance Israelis attached to this vote. Before the election, many observers were saying that it was one of the most consequential – if not the most consequential – votes, and clearly many Israelis felt the same way. What drove this high turnout was different types of fears. Israelis of all persuasions were worried about how the outcome would affect what kind of country Israel becomes. The second big takeaway is that the ruling coalition, formed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu after the 2022 election, was resoundingly rejected by the majority of Israeli voters – well over 50% cast their vote for parties opposed to the current government. Likud supporters at an election night event in Jerusalem, Israel. Alexi J. Rosenfeld/Getty Images The five parties that make up Netanyahu’s right-wing and religious coalition went into the election with 68 seats in the 120-seat parliament. That same bloc will now have 53 – and that is a significant loss, no matter how Netanyahu tries to spin this as a victory. It means that those five parties will not be able to form the next government, and as such, the vote stands as a repudiation of the Netanyahu government. Netanyahu’s Likud party will still be the largest in parliament. But its share of the national vote declined, and it looks like it will have six fewer seats in the next parliament, another blow to Netanyahu. Netanyahu’s far-right coalition partners fared worse than expected, too. In part, this was due to “wasted votes” going to a new far-right party that failed to make it above the 3.25% of the national vote needed to be represented in parliament. Also, Likud drew some voters away from these far-right parties who had voted for them in the last election. What drove the Arab parties’ surprise showing? The performance of the Arab majority parties – the more secular and left-wing Joint List and the more religious and conservative United Arab List – is very important. Combined, they currently look to have increased their representation by nine seats, bringing their total to 19, a historic high for them. The reason for that is the massive turnout of Arab voters – much higher than the last election. But also, a less noticed trend is the increase in Jewish votes that those parties received. It is important to note that these are Arab-majority parties, not simply Arab parties. Israeli left-wing protesters call for the formation of a government including Arab parties. Ilia Yefimovich/AFP via Getty Images Aside from Netanyahu, it was also a disappointing result for the main opposition party, Yashar; its leader, Gadi Eisenkot; and the anti-Netanyahu Change Bloc it was part of. The preelection polls suggested that the Zionist opposition bloc would do slightly better than the ruling coalition bloc. But Yashar ended up with over 200,000 fewer votes than Likud, winning a projected 21 seats compared to Likud’s 26, and the “Change Bloc” is heading to 48 seats, far short of a parliamentary majority. Ultimately, what is clear is that the Israeli public remains deeply divided. And the fact that there is still a good chance that Netanyahu will emerge as prime minister is remarkable given that many observers had already written his political obituary after the Oct. 7 attack. Was the vote a referendum on Netanyahu? Certainly many saw this as a referendum on Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister. For his supporters, Netanyahu is the only person to be trusted with Israel’s security, especially given the threat from Iran. They credit him for weakening – albeit not defeating – the two non-state actors that most threaten Israeli security, Hezbollah and Hamas, and they praise him for ensuring President Donald Trump’s support for Israel. But for those who voted against Netanyahu, the fact that he has refused to take any personal responsibility for the Oct. 7 security failure – amid reports that he had advance warning of a major planned Hamas attack – factored into his poor election showing, as did his government’s refusal to establish a state commission of inquiry to investigate the Oct. 7 security failings. Many also blame Netanyahu for not prioritizing the release of the Israeli hostages held in Gaza and prolonging the war there. He is also held responsible by many for the precipitous decline in Israel’s international standing and for jeopardizing Israel’s crucial alliance with the United States. But it was domestic issues, rather than external ones, that motivated many of those who voted for anti-Netanyahu parties. Many fear that democracy in Israel is under attack, and they particularly oppose the effort by Netanyahu’s government to weaken the power and independence of the Israeli judiciary, which sparked massive street protests in 2023. They also strongly resent that Netanyahu’s government has allowed ultra-Orthodox men to avoid military service, despite the Israeli military’s growing manpower shortage. And on a personal level, Netanyahu is widely perceived as self-serving and dishonest – he is still on trial for corruption. Arab voters have other, more specific concerns that drove them to vote in record numbers, in addition to the Netanyahu government’s policies in Gaza and the West Bank, which they strongly oppose. Chief among them is the soaring rates of violent crime in their communities, which the government – particularly the far-right Itamar Ben-Gvir, who oversees the police – has done nothing to address, say his critics. More broadly, many Palestinian-Arab citizens of Israel fear that if the far-right parties remained in power, their civil rights would be under threat. What should we expect next? The key thing to underline is what happens on election day in Israel is just the first stage in the process of forming a new government. Since no party ever receives a majority of seats in the parliament, what really matters is what happens after the election when the coalition building begins. This can take weeks, if not longer. The party with the largest number of seats typically gets the first chance to assemble a governing coalition, but not always. Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, will choose who gets the first chance to form a government based on who is most likely to succeed. Right now, it looks like Eisenkot will get the first opportunity, but his only real option is to form a minority government that would depend on the parliamentary support of the Arab-majority parties – which some members of his Change Bloc adamantly oppose. Former Israeli military chief and Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot waves an Israeli flag as he addresses supporters on Oct. 28, 2026. Tomer Neuberg/Middle East Images/AFP via Getty Images Despite the success of the Arab-majority parties in the election, it is unlikely they will be invited to be formal members of any coalition – although that has happened once in the past, when the United Arab List joined the short-lived government of 2021-22 led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid. If Eisenkot is unable to form a government, then Netanyahu will get the chance. He could try to entice some leaders of the parties in the Change bloc to defect and join a right-wing government under his leadership, or a broader “national unity” government with a rotating leader. Netanyahu did that in the past with Benny Gantz, but then he later prevented Gantz from becoming prime minister – so I doubt Eisenkot would agree to do this with Netanyahu. There are reports in the media that the Trump administration would like a national unity government in Israel, so that might increase the pressure on Eisenkot to accept this outcome. And should war with Iran heat up again, that would increase the pressure. The most likely scenario, I believe, is that neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot will be able to form a government, and a new election will be called, with Netanyahu as caretaker prime minister until that vote. Netanyahu has reason to hope that his bloc will do better in another election, so that may well be his game plan. In which case, it will be many months until Israel has a new government. 05fbd3b81be964a0: From Martin Vengadesan
I couldn’t help but be struck by the contrasting leadership styles on display in the run-up to the Melaka polls.
While neither is a candidate for chief minister, both PKR’s Adam Adli and Umno’s Dr Akmal Saleh are the faces of the future for their respective parties.
To me, Adam of PKR displays a soft-spoken, progressive style. There is backbone to his principles, and he was a student leader who was detained and harassed by the previous regime.
He chose to join a multiracial party and has progressed from PKR Youth chief to deputy minister of higher education after winning the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary seat.
While he often comes under the cosh over the failed PTPTN loan abolition, I have seen him at work trying to extend the benefits of our nation to its less fortunate.
On the other hand, there’s the rabble-rousing Akmal of Umno. The two men were born a year apart but represent very different ways of thinking.
Indeed, his career reads to me like a hall of shame. But presumably, it has some appeal among the rempit crowd.

Just last week came another defamation suit loss, as the Melaka High Court ruled in Teresa Kok’s favour over his September 2024 remarks slamming her for questioning a proposed mandatory halal certification.
Kok was awarded RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages, plus RM50,000 in costs. He had called her an “old Nyonya” and suggested placing a non-halal logo on her forehead.

Now he says he is prepared to give up his bid to defend the Merlimau state seat in the Melaka election on Nov 14 if the court case he faces over a charge under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code hurts Umno and Barisan Nasional’s chances at the polls.
Akmal is charged with making statements on his Facebook page that allegedly caused public fear, alarm, or disruption to public order.
The charge stems from a viral Facebook video and post made around Aug 11, 2025, regarding an incident in which the Jalur Gemilang was displayed upside down.
Akmal said he had conveyed his position to Umno president Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, stressing that the party’s interests must come before his personal ambitions.
This is, of course, merely the latest transgression by a man who has positioned himself as an ethnic champion. Akmal was also previously involved in a defamation suit brought by his sibling.

In 2024, he called on the prime minister to sack tourism, arts and culture minister Tiong King Sing after bak kut teh was recognised as a national heritage food. In the same year, he was involved in a dispute over vernacular schools that led to an insinuation that his opponent, P Ramasamy, was drunk.
And of course he led the KK Mart boycott campaign after socks bearing the word “Allah” were discovered on sale there. Is his brand of politics toxic or constructive? I leave you to decide.

Adam has been working quietly to build consensus. The fact that he cares about all Malaysians does not make him any less of a member of his race or religion. In fact, that is one of the great false assumptions in Malaysian public life.
In his roles at the higher education ministry and the youth and sports ministry, Adam has supported several public-facing initiatives, including PTPTN loan repayment flexibility.

Under the repayment measures announced in the 2027 budget, borrowers earning between RM2,501 and RM3,000 a month are required to make minimum monthly payments of RM50, while those earning below RM2,500 a month are eligible for repayment exemptions.

Other initiatives for students include support for transit passes like My50 and MyKomuter50, alongside the FlySiswa flight subsidy of RM500 for students who travel between Peninsular Malaysia and East Malaysia.
He has promoted technical and vocational education and training (TVET) to bolster graduate employability and supported the revival of the Rakan Muda programme for youth development.
He has also been involved in local infrastructure and welfare projects in Hang Tuah Jaya, such as local flood mitigation.
More than anything else, he views the future with a keen mind and open heart. These are the leaders we need if we are to stop going around in circles.
Martin Vengadesan is a former editor who currently serves as a strategic communications consultant to the communications ministry.

7929e6ff65cd98ce: Shares in Google’s parent company Alphabet dived by almost ten percent on Wednesday, after the web giant admitted AI-powered searches earn it less money than it earns by serving ads with its old-school search engine.

Alphabet on Wednesday reported its Q3 results, which included news that its year-over-year search query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years. Some of that growth comes from users adopting “AI Mode” – Google’s latest LLM-powered search system.
Google’s revenue from search rose 12 percent year-over-year to $63.25 billion, a little lower than the 14.5 percent growth the company reported in last year’s Q3.
During Alphabet’s earnings call, chief business officer Philipp Schindler said the slowdown was caused by “lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode.”

That’s a worry given that Google is spending enormous sums on infrastructure. $51.4 billion went out the door in Q3, around two thirds of it going towards servers and networking equipment. The rest funded datacenter builds.

That spending appears to have impacted profitability, as Alphabet reported $26.17 billion net income for the quarter. Last year’s Q3, during which Google revenue was $102.35 billion, produced $35 billion net income.
Schindler argued that AI search will pay off.

“On AI Mode, many of these queries are upper funnel queries, allowing us to capture new, high-value commercial intent,” he told investors. “In addition, the majority of AI Mode queries are incremental, creating more monetization opportunities over time.”
Google tried to seize one of those opportunities today, by turning on ads alongside AI Mode searches around the world, after first testing them in the US only.
But for now, AI Mode searches aren’t as lucrative as Google’s existing search business, which brought in just under half of Alphabet's $125.8 billion quarterly revenue.

Google’s cloud is its next-best earner, at $24.75 billion for the quarter, but it has troubles too because the Big G doesn’t have enough capacity to serve all its customers. The company has started to offload some customer workloads to third parties, and warned that will dent its future margins.

Thomas Kurian, Google Cloud’s CEO, said the company has over 100 companies using its TPU silicon, adding that “All of the inventory for TPU systems are associated with committed contracts” – meaning Google can see some revenue to cover some capex. The company expects to book revenue from TPU sales to third parties in coming quarters.

CEO Sundar Pichai was full of optimism for future AI revenue, noting that Google’s Gemini app has won a billion users faster than any other product in the company’s history, and praising the performance of its models. He said Google is moving fast to create agentic AI tools, but will focus on business customers for starters, “because the bar for security, safety, and governance is extremely high.”
“As a next step, we are bringing these features to Search and also, of course, to our billion users on the Gemini app,” he added.
Pichai didn’t say when agentic AI will come to search or if he expects it will avoid the monetization issues AI Mode has already caused.
Yet the company also stuck to its $195-$205 billion capital expenditure forecast for this year and said it intends to spend “significantly” more in 2027. ®

270aee5ea45a14da: Melihat senarai calon wanita untuk PRN Melaka saya sebetulnya terkedu. Ia cepat membawa saya kepada watak-watak wanita ikonik dalam sejarah Kesultanan Melayu Melaka. Sukar untuk memadam watak-watak seperti Tun Kudu, Tun Teja dan Tun Fatimah dari benak. Malangnya wanita yang saya sebutkan ini dihinjak dalam politik.

Ambil sahaja Tun Kudu yang menjadi sekadar 'alat' untuk kepentingan penguasa. Tun Kudu adalah puteri kepada Bendahara Seri Wak Raja dan merupakan permaisuri kepada Sultan Muzaffar Syah yang memerintah Melaka (1446-1459). Namun demikian untuk meredakan perseteruan dua kem politik orang Melayu yang berebutkan kedudukan sebagai bendahara, Sultan Muzzafar Syah telah menceraikan Tun Kudu dan mengaturkan baginda untuk menjadi isteri Bendahara Seri Nara Diraja yang sudah tua kerepot, lagi berusia.

Seri Nara Diraja memang menyebabkan Sultan Muzaffar sakit kepala kerana enggan bersara, membolot jawatan tersebut setelah Bendahara Seri Wak Raja dan hanya sedia melakukannya dengan syarat diberi hadiah gundik sultan. Makanya dalam percaturan Sultan Muzaffar, Paduka Raja Tun Perak, iaitu kekanda Tun Kudu terpaksa mengambil sikap damai. Tun Ali atau Seri Nara Diraja itu adalah bapa saudara Sultan Muzaffar Syah dan pembesar yang bertanggungjawab mengatur dan meletakkan Sultan Muzaffar di atas takhta pada 1446.

Watak kedua pula adalah Tun Teja iaitu anak Bendahara Pahang Seri Amar Bangsa Diraja dan disebut sebagai tunangan kepada Sultan Pahang, Sultan Abdul Jalil. Akan tetapi Sultan Mahmud Syah yang gila perempuan telah berusaha mendapatkan Tun Teja lantas bertitah kepada pembesar; "Barang siapa membawa anak Bendahara Pahang itu ke mari, apa yang dikehendakinya ku anugerahkan akan dia. Jikalau ia hendakkan sekerat kota dengan kerajaan sekalipun kita anugerahkan".

Dalam riwayat, Tun Teja dilarikan oleh Hang Nadim (menantu kepada Laksamana Hang Tuah) demi menebus kesalahannya terhadap sultan. Untuk melakukannya, Hang Nadim merasuah seorang pelulut untuk memujuk Tun Teja agar kelak berkahwin dengan Sultan Mahmud Syah. Berdasarkan Hikayat Hang Tuah, Tun Teja merupakan seorang yang bermaruah tinggi dan bukanlah gilakan kedudukan. Beliau malah menolak lamaran sultan Melaka, sebaliknya memilih menjadi isteri Megat Panji Alam Terengganu.
Perbuatan pelulut membujuk Tun Teja ini gagal. Oleh sebab Tun Teja liat dan berkeras, malangnya baginda disihir dengan ubat guna-guna lantas dipaksa berkahwin dengan Sultan Mahmud tanpa kerelaan.

Sultan Mahmud Syah selaku raja dan sultan yang gila perempuan seterusnya mensasarkan pula Tun Fatimah. Baginda adalah anak Tun Mutahir dan baru berkahwin dengan Tun Ali. Sultan Mahmud Syah menggunakan kuasa baginda untuk membunuh Tun Ali sebelum merebut Tun Fatimah. Ini juga didorong oleh fitnah Raja Mendaliar kononnya Tun Mutahir sedang merancang untuk menggulingkannya. Sultan menitahkan Tun Sura Diraja dan Tun Indera Segara untuk menghabisi seisi keluarga bendahara. Kesan atau trauma kehilangan seisi keluarga dan suami itu, Tun Fatimah hidup berendam dendam. Dalam riwayat disebut Tun Fatimah itu 'selama ia duduk dengan Sultan Mahmud Syah jangankan ia tertawa, tersenyum pun tiada pernah'. Bahkan setiap kali mengandung, baginda menggugurkan kandungannya.

Kisah raja gila seks, termakan fitnah dan pertelingkahan politik antara kem pembesar untuk berebut kedudukan dan jawatan bendahara ini adalah satu renungan yang penting untuk kita memahami pula konteks semasa.

Hari ini Melaka menyaksikan sekali lagi perebutan kuasa dalam bentuk pilihan raya. Dengan mengambil ingatan, Melaka melayan watak wanita sebagai alat percaturan politik, pemuas nafsu dan sekadar di pinggiran; saya dengan berhati-hati mencari parti politik yang tidak melakukan hal-hal sedemikian. Saya juga menyuruhkan kaum keluarga saya yang terdiri dari pengundi wanita untuk tidak memilih mereka yang melayan wanita dengan buruk.

Sudah tentu kita telah menjauhi era kesultanan Melayu yang penuh malapetaka seperti di atas. Iklim politik kita juga harapnya tidaklah setoksik itu. Pun tenung punya tenung saya mesti memastikan parti politik manakah yang tidak menjadikan wanita sekadar melukut di tepi gantang. Saya benci perlakuan Melaka di zaman lampau tersebut.

Mengapakah saya memberi tumpuan kepada wanita? Jawapan mudahnya, ini adalah kerana dalam rekod, terdapat 348,849 orang pengundi di PRN Melaka kali ini adalah perempuan, iaitu 50.73% daripada jumlah keseluruhan pemilih. Justeru saya berpandangan penting untuk kita melihat komponen parti manakah yang paling bersungguh memperjuangkan wanita.

Letak duduk wanita dalam politik adalah penting terutama setelah ucapan kontroversi di Persidangan Agung Umno 2026, iaitu apabila Presiden Zahid Hamidi berseloroh mengatakan Ketua Wanita Noraini Ahmad nampak macam 'nenek-nenek'.

Pakatan Harapan menjanjikan lima orang calon wanita untuk membawa mandat rakyat Melaka di kawasan masing-masing. Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) mengetengahkan tiga orang calon wanita dalam PRN Melaka, pada 14 November ini. Menurut Setiausaha Agung Fuziah Salleh, daripada sembilan calon yang diketengahkan parti itu, tiga calon wanita telah diberi kepercayaan untuk bertanding, dan ini mewakili 33.3% daripada keseluruhan calon PKR pada PRN. Calon wanita ini adalah Ketua Pemuda Tangga Batu, Farzana Hayani Nasir di Klebang; Ketua Penerangan Wanita Ginie Lim Siew Lin yang sekali lagi bertanding di DUN Machap Jaya, dan Esma Eazreen Husin di Rim. Farzana, seorang Gen Z baru-baru ini mendapat perhatian ramai apabila diusir seorang anggota wanita Umno dari menghadiri program Kampung Angkat Madani di kawasan masjid Bukit Rambai.

Dalam pada itu, Amanah di Merlimau membawakan Rahayu Hamzah. Beliau akan membawa tugas besar untuk menewaskan Ketua Pemuda Umno, Dr Akmal Saleh yang baru-baru ini kalah dalam saman berkaitan isu cadangan pensijilan halal, di mana Akmal merujuk Ahli Parlimen Seputeh, Teresa Kok sebagai 'nyonya tua'. Akmal diperintahkan membayar ganti rugi berjumlah RM250,000 kepada Teresa. Ini termasuklah kos perundangan sebanyak RM50,000 (jumlah keseluruhan RM300,000). Dalam vonis hakim, iaitu Isa Aziz Ibrahim; Akmal malah ditegur dengan kata-kata bahawa adab itu membentuk keperibadian.

Menariknya jumlah peratusan pengundi wanita di DUN N.27 Merlimau, Melaka ini adalah sebanyak 52.45% berdasarkan data rasmi Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya Malaysia. Justeru kita akan mengetahui minda atau kognitif pengundi wanita di Merlimau, bagaimana mereka melayan wanita itu sendiri. Apakah misalnya 'adab membentuk keperibadian' akan dijadikan pedoman.
Sebuah lagi parti komponen Pakatan Harapan, DAP pula menaruh harapan menerusi Leng Chau Yen yang bertanding di kerusi DUN N22 Bandar Hilir.

Umno terus tampil meletakkan calon-calon lelaki yang berusia di kebanyakan kerusi. Parti ini juga sekadar meletakkan tiga calon wanita untuk bertanding. Hal ini tentulah menyedihkan. Calon wanita dikemukakan di Pengkalan Batu (menggugurkan penyandang wanita sebelum ini yang agak cekatan). Dalam pada itu, muka lama Tuminah Kadi dikitar semula di Pantai Kundor; sementara bekas pengacara rancangan hiburan dikekalkan di Rim, iaitu Khaidhirah anak ketua menteri Melaka kelapan, Abu Zahar Ithnin.

Adalah menarik untuk kita melihat bagaimana hampir separuh pengundi wanita di Melaka kelak mengundi. Yakni apakah mereka akan membiarkan watak seperti Tun Teja, Tun Kudu dan Tun Fatimah menjadi igauan politik di Melaka; atau melakukan sesuatu yang beradab.

bea6ae276ae0bb55: When a child refuses to share a table with another child because one eats pork, we are no longer talking about a minor classroom incident. We are talking about a failure of national education.
Malaysia’s schools are now producing children who see difference as contamination, faith as a barrier, and fellow Malaysians as people to be avoided.
This is not unity. It is segregation being taught early, quietly and dangerously.
A warning from the classroom

Puncak Borneo MP Willie Mongin recently revealed that some primary school pupils had refused to sit beside classmates of another faith. Among the reasons were that a classmate was eating pork or wearing a cross.
Let that sink in.
Children young enough to still be learning multiplication tables are already being taught, directly or indirectly, that another child’s food, religion or symbol makes them unworthy of friendship.
Do not hide behind the excuse that “children repeat what they hear at home”. Of course, families matter.
But schools are where society either corrects prejudice or normalises it. If a child can carry such intolerance into a classroom without being firmly challenged, then the classroom has failed.
Unity cannot remain a slogan
For decades, Malaysia has recited the Rukun Negara, held unity-themed assemblies and printed national slogans on walls, banners and exercise books.
Yet what is the value of a national principle if a child will not sit beside another child because of what that child eats or believes?

The Rukun Negara is not decoration. It is not a mural. It is not a slogan for official events. If it means anything, it must be visible in how children treat one another every day, in classrooms, canteens, playgrounds and school buses.
Our education system has become too comfortable with symbolism. It celebrates diversity on stage but often fails to build genuine relationships across communities in daily school life.
Separate childhoods, divided futures
Malaysia’s national, Chinese and Tamil primary schools reflect our multicultural reality. Preserving mother tongues and cultural identity is legitimate and necessary.
But preserving identity must not mean raising children in social isolation.

When pupils spend their formative years largely among those who look, pray, eat and speak like them, anything different becomes unfamiliar. And unfamiliarity easily induces fear. Fear becomes prejudice. Prejudice breeds rejection.
How can we expect adults to build a united Malaysia if, as children, they were never given real opportunities to know one another?

Joint sports, debates, arts, science projects, community service and shared classrooms must not be occasional photo opportunities. They must be routine, structured and compulsory parts of school life, not pleasing politicians for their occasional visit to school.
Stop pretending the system is fair
We must also stop pretending that education policy is neutral.
For too long, access to opportunities, scholarships, school placements and pathways has been viewed through racial lenses.
Whatever the original intention, the consequence is clear: many young Malaysians grow up believing that their future depends more on their ethnicity than their effort, talent or need.

Helping the disadvantaged is right. But assistance must be transparent, needs-based and accountable. A system that leaves one community feeling privileged and another feeling excluded cannot claim to be building unity.
A child who believes the system does not value them equally will not easily believe the nation values them equally.
Malaysia built on community effort

Our history lessons must stop being exercises in memorising dates and names. They must teach the harder truth: Malaysia was built through negotiation, compromise and cooperation among communities that did not always share the same faith, language or customs.
Tunku Abdul Rahman, Tun Tan Siew Sin and Tun VT Sambanthan came from different communities, yet they worked towards one national objective: independence.
If our founding leaders could sit at the same table and build a nation, why should a child today refuse to sit beside a classmate because of pork or a cross?
No community owns Malaysia. Every community helped build it. Every community has a stake in protecting it.
The education ministry must answer
This is not a problem to be passed to the national unity ministry while the education ministry (MoE) hides behind curriculum documents.
The MoE must answer directly:
Why are children absorbing religious intolerance in schools?
Are teachers trained to identify and confront prejudice early?
Are schools required to create meaningful interaction across communities?
Are incidents of discrimination investigated, recorded and corrected?
Are school leaders held accountable when unity exists only in speeches?
If the ministry cannot enforce the values it preaches, then it is not merely failing pupils. It is failing Malaysia.
Make unity measurable
National unity must become part of every subject, every school and every level of education.
Kindergartens must teach children to play, share and cooperate across backgrounds. Primary and secondary schools must run regular joint programmes with schools of different streams.
History, literature and civics must teach shared nationhood, not narrow narratives. Group work must deliberately bring children out of familiar ethnic and religious circles.

Teachers need training in inclusive classroom practices, religious literacy and conflict resolution. Textbook writers must be held accountable for accuracy, balance and the removal of stereotypes, not mere focus on any one community.
And the ministry must publish measurable indicators: pupils’ sense of belonging, participation in cross-community activities, teacher preparedness, complaints handled and corrective action taken.
Unity must be assessed, not merely announced.
The future is sitting in our classrooms
A child who refuses to share a table today may become an adult who refuses to share a country tomorrow.
This is the harsh truth Malaysia must face: our education system is not merely underperforming academically; it is failing in its duty to mould Malaysians.

We can continue producing students with excellent grades but shallow citizenship. Or we can rebuild schools into places where children learn that faith, food, language and culture must never determine who deserves their friendship.
Malaysia’s future will not be decided only in parliament or boardrooms. It will be decided at classroom tables, where children either learn to see one another as strangers, or as fellow Malaysians.
